On Sunday’s early trading session, the market clarified its stance with a single bearish candle.

BTC $76,086, down 1.85%; ETH $2,389, down 2.03%. On the surface, it’s a pullback; underneath, the structure is speaking.

━━━ Current system readings ━━━
BTC is nominally BULL_TREND, but inside, the number of bearish votes has already overtaken. ETH is even more direct—CHOP_MID; it’s grinding out a bottom in a range, with no clear direction yet. This disagreement isn’t a contradiction—it’s the market arranging the cards for its next move.

━━━ Psychological layer ━━━
Weekend moves are where people most easily make two mistakes: one is seeing it drop and rushing to buy the dip, thinking it’s cheap now; the other is seeing it drop and immediately going bearish, assuming the trend has reversed. Both are emotion trading, not judgment trading. True discipline is: when the system hasn’t changed, the strategy doesn’t change; when the system changes, switch immediately. That’s it—what’s hard is execution.

━━━ Strategy direction ━━━
BTC direction: wait for structural confirmation before acting; don’t chase the selloff; don’t grab snap rebounds. ETH: treat it with a light position within the range system; don’t trade it as a trend.

I’ve seen too many fake breakouts on weekends. Let’s talk after Monday’s European session opens.

#BTC #ETH #Contract trading

Have miners finally turned the corner? Bitcoin hashprice surges 20.41% in four days to a new high since May

Miner revenue metric hashprice has risen 20.41% over four days, and miners’ cash flow has clearly rebounded.

Hashprice is the core metric for how much miners can earn per unit of hashrate. It factors in the coin price, transaction fees, and the network difficulty. Over the past four days, this metric has jumped 20.41%, returning to the highest level seen since May. Put simply, this round of BTC price rebound has lifted miners’ unit earnings directly. In recent months, miners’ days have been tough: weak coin prices combined with difficulty levels at the high end have squeezed profit margins thin. Many mining firms have been forced to sell coins to survive, and some even cut hashrate or shut down operations. With hashprice rising, it’s as if the entire mining industry has been given a shot of life.

Market impact
- Short term: Miners’ selling pressure will ease. After profits recover, mining firms won’t be forced to dump the coins they mine, reducing the passive selling pressure from miners. Around the BTC $76,338 area, this provides tangible support to the trading picture.
- Medium term: A rebound in hashprice will delay hashrate centralization and the clearing out of weaker players. Medium and smaller mining firms can last a bit longer. If the coin price holds steady, mining stocks (MARA, RIOT, etc.)’s earnings expectations may also improve.

My view
I treat this data as a lagging confirmation signal rather than a leading signal—hashprice is rising because the coin price is rising, not the other way around. But it has a second-order implication: miners are shifting from being sellers to hoarders, improving the structure of sell-side pressure on the supply side. BTC is currently around $76,338. As long as it doesn’t fall back into the dense cost basis zone, and miners don’t restart selling, the foundation for this rebound is stronger than before. The risk is that if the coin price pulls back and the hashprice gains are given back, selling pressure will return immediately. Directionally, I’m moderately bullish on this piece of news—it’s a positive confirmation type.

Over the past few months, miners have been struggling—weak coin prices, high difficulty, and squeezed profits from both ends. When it goes up, you want to chase—that’s the first layer of thinking.

The second layer is to ask one question: who is selling?

In *The Most Important Thing in Investing*, Howard repeatedly talks about the second layer of thinking.

Today, $ETH 2,373; in the past 24 hours it’s down 2.73%, with trading volume of 844 million USDT.

In a slow, downward drifting market, buyers aren’t panicking, and sellers aren’t stopping.

These more-than-8 billion in volume can’t be dumped by retail traders.

First-layer thinking sees: “It’s down—run quickly.”

Second-layer thinking sees: “At this level, what is the seller switching to?”

The book gives an example.

First-layer thinking says: “The company is good—buy.”

Second-layer thinking says: “The company is good, but if everyone says it’s good, then the price is expensive.”

Swap “company” with $ETH and it’s the same.

I won’t guess the direction, but this question is more interesting than the candlestick chart.

I saved this—I'll verify it later.

ETF inflows of $492 million, but contract positions are still shrinking: BTC/ETH—who are they waiting for to take a stance?

Behind $BTC and $ETH, net ETF inflows of $492 million have just appeared, yet prices are falling and open interest is still contracting. Why didn’t spot inflows turn into a chase higher?

The facts: In Binance USDT-margined perpetuals, $BTC in the past 24 hours is at $76,136, down 1.59%, with turnover of about $8.74 billion; $ETH is at $2,375, down 2.69%, with turnover of about $8.70 billion. Both contracts are in TRADING status, and BTC’s latest funding rate is around 1.00 basis points.

Funding reality: In Farside’s August 21 data, US spot BTC ETFs saw net inflows of $307.5 million and ETH ETFs had net inflows of $184.0 million, totaling about $491.5 million. This shows allocation capital is still coming in. However, the data reflects the previous trading day’s subscription/redemption results—not buy pressure occurring every minute right now.

Live perps show another picture. Over the past two hours, BTC’s open interest notional is about -0.25%, and ETH about -1.34%. Prices are weakening and positions are shrinking—this looks more like both long and short sides are reducing risk, not that shorts have won unilaterally. The ETF tailwind hasn’t failed; it’s just acting on a different time scale than contract deleveraging.

Hypothesis: The market is confirming two things. First, whether ETF allocation capital can support spot when weekend liquidity is thin. Second, after contract positions come down, whether buyers are willing to re-enter. The most common mistake ordinary traders make is using yesterday’s ETF inflows to explain every single short-term intraday candlestick today—then chasing price higher under elevated funding rates.

For the bulls to be confirmed: price needs to first stop falling, trading activity needs to rebound, open interest should rise again in a modest and steady way, and the funding rate should not keep climbing. For the bears to be confirmed: BTC and ETH need to break further lower, volume should expand, and falling positions still can’t halt the downtrend—meaning it’s not just simple short de-leveraging; spot demand/absorption is also weakening. Until both sides are confirmed, the value of directional calls is lower than position/risk control.

My view: I lean toward watching the first increase in positioning after deleveraging ends. If both price and positions repair together, the bullish case is complete; if positions rise but price keeps falling, the bears have more control. Risk warning: weekend depth is thinner, leverage can amplify slippage and fast reversals—keep risk light and set stop-losses in advance.

$BTC、$ETH背后刚出现4.92亿美元ETF净流入，价格却下跌、合约仓位还在收缩：现货利好为什么没有换来追涨？

事实：Binance U本位永续里，$BTC近24小时报76,136美元、变动-1.59%，成交约87.4亿美元；$ETH报2,375美元、变动-2.69%，成交约87.0亿美元。两者合约状态均为TRADING，BTC最新资金费率约1.00个基点。

资金事实：Farside的8月21日数据中，美国现货BTC ETF净流入3.075亿美元，ETH ETF净流入1.840亿美元，合计约4.915亿美元。这证明配置资金仍在进入，但数据对应的是上一交易日申赎结果，不是此刻每一分钟都在发生的买盘。

实时合约给出另一幅图。最近两小时，BTC未平仓名义价值约-0.25%，ETH约-1.34%。价格走弱、持仓收缩，更像多空双方都在减风险，而不是空头单方面取得胜利。ETF利好没有失效，只是它和合约去杠杆处在不同时间尺度。

推测：市场正在确认两件事。第一，ETF配置资金能否在周末流动性偏薄时托住现货；第二，合约仓位降下来以后，买盘是否愿意重新进场。普通交易者最容易犯的错，是拿昨天的ETF流入去解释今天每一根短线K线，随后在高资金费率下追着价格跑。

多头成立，需要价格先止跌，成交回升，未平仓量重新温和增加，同时资金费率不继续抬高。空头成立，需要BTC、ETH继续破低，成交放大，而持仓下降仍止不住跌势；那说明不是简单清杠杆，而是现货承接也在变弱。两边都没确认前，方向判断的价值低于仓位控制。

我的观点：我更偏向观察去杠杆结束后的第一次持仓回升。如果价格与持仓一起修复，多头证据才完整；如果持仓回升但价格继续跌，空头更占主动。风险提示：周末深度较薄，杠杆会放大滑点和快速反向，轻仓并预设止损。

U.S. banking industry lobbying groups are calling for KYC obligations to be extended from stablecoin issuers to exchanges, directly impacting retail inflow and outflow processes.

The Bank Policy Institute (BPI) submitted a comment letter to FinCEN on behalf of large U.S. banks. Its core request is this: stablecoin issuers must currently perform customer identity verification (CIP), but the secondary market—i.e., the stage where retail users buy and sell stablecoins on exchanges—has no equivalent requirement. Plainly put, banks want their compliance costs to become the industry’s compliance costs.

Iran warns of retaliation against US economic interests: risk-aversion returns, putting short-term pressure on BTC

Iran threatens to target US economic interests over new sanctions; prospects for US-Iran negotiations cool down, and risk-off sentiment weighs on BTC.

The US adds further sanctions against Iran, and Iran’s officials directly say they will retaliate against the US’s economic interests. Those words are quite severe—effectively closing off half the door to diplomatic talks. The market previously had some expectation of a US-Iran agreement before 2026, but that outlook is rapidly fading. The geopolitical risk premium is returning, and funds begin shifting toward safe-haven assets.

Market impact
The transmission path is straightforward: Iran’s threat → expectations of heightened tension in the Strait of Hormuz → oil price fluctuations → reduced risk appetite in US equities → the crypto market absorbs selling pressure. BTC is currently $76,565.53 (24h -0.51%), ETH $2,413.47 (-0.09%). The drawdown isn’t large, but the move is in the same direction—suggesting a sentiment-driven drift lower rather than a panic sell-off.

- Short term: Under the geopolitical risk-aversion logic, funds withdraw from high-risk assets; BTC is unlikely to form an independent move and will most likely track broader risk assets lower
- Medium term: If sanctions keep escalating and negotiations completely break down, the 2026 agreement outlook becomes invalid—leaving fewer macro tailwinds as a bullish catalyst

My view
Slightly bearish in the short term. BTC around $76,500 can still hold up, but if it breaks down, the next support level to watch will be the prior low area. $78,000 is a rebound resistance; it will be difficult to break through while tensions with Iran remain elevated. ETH is relatively resilient (-0.09%), but if BTC underperforms further, the probability of ETH following lower is higher than that of independent strength. Geopolitical conflict has always been a double-edged sword for BTC’s “digital gold” narrative: in the short run, BTC is sold off as a risk asset first. Safe-haven capital still prefers gold and US Treasuries. I lean toward waiting and watching for stabilization—neither chasing shorts nor urgently buying.

Iran threatens retaliation over US economic interests, risk aversion heats up; BTC clings to 76K

Iran has openly threatened US economic interests, increasing the risk of a breakdown in talks between the two sides. Risk-aversion sentiment has weighed on BTC to $76,565.

The US has added another batch of sanctions against Iran, and Iran responded directly: it will target US economic interests. This isn’t just empty talk—oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and shipping routes near US military bases in the Middle East could all be potential targets. The key issue is timing: the market originally expected that by before 2026, the US and Iran could agree on some de-escalation plan, but that expectation has essentially been dashed. The diplomatic window is narrowing, and the geopolitical risk premium is back in the pricing.

Market impact
Let’s make the transmission path clear: escalation in Middle East conflict → surge in oil prices → higher US inflation expectations → reduced room for the Fed to cut rates → tighter liquidity expectations → downward pressure on BTC. BTC is not a safe-haven asset; it’s a liquidity asset. When geopolitical tensions rise, it falls along with US equities rather than rallying like gold.

- Short term: BTC at $76,565 (24h -0.51%) has started showing signs of a pullback. ETH at $2,413 (-0.09%) has held up relatively better, but only with a lag—not immunity. If oil jumps higher, risk assets will be under pressure across the board.
- Medium term: the expectation of a US-Iran deal in 2026 has failed, meaning the entire 2026 macro storyline needs rewriting. The rate-cut path may come later and be shallower, which would suppress valuations.

My view
Bearish. In the short term, whether BTC can hold the 76K whole-number level is crucial. A breakdown would open room to the downside. Support lies around $74K–$75K; resistance is at 78K. If ETH ($2,413) loses $2,400, the next look is around $2,300. Scenario analysis: if Iran is only posturing, the market may digest the impact within about a week. But if it actually strikes oil tankers or blocks the Strait of Hormuz, the risk-aversion mode would fully kick in and the drawdown for risk assets would not be small. I currently lean toward the first scenario, but position-wise I still want to leave room for the latter.

One-sentence translation: Geopolitical risk doesn’t directly smash the market—it gradually tightens liquidity through the path of “inflation rising → rate cuts delayed,” and BTC’s valuation depends on liquidity.

传导路径说清楚：中东冲突升级→油价飙升→美国通胀预期抬头→美联储降息空间被压缩→流动性预期收紧→BTC承压。BTC不是避险资产，它是流动性资产，地缘紧张时它跟着美股跌，不跟黄金涨。

- 短期：BTC报$76,565（24h -0.51%），已现回调苗头。ETH $2,413（-0.09%）相对抗跌，但只是滞后，不是免疫。若油价跳涨，风险资产全线承压。
- 中期：2026年美伊协议预期落空，意味着整个2026年的宏观剧本要重写，降息路径可能更晚更浅，压制估值。

利空。BTC短期看76K整数关口能不能守住，跌破打开下行空间，下方支撑看74K-75K区域；反弹阻力78K。ETH $2,413失守$2,400的话看$2,300。情景推演：伊朗只是嘴炮→影响一周内消化；真动手打了油轮或封锁霍尔木兹海峡→避险模式全开，风险资产跌幅不会小。目前我倾向前一种，但仓位上要为后一种留余地。

一句话翻译：地缘风险不是直接砸盘，是通过“通胀抬头→降息推迟”这条路慢慢掐住流动性，BTC的估值靠的就是流动性。

BSTR Terminates Cantor SPAC Merger Plan; Bitcoin Treasury Listing Called Off

BSTR Holdings, a Bitcoin treasury company supported by Adam Back, has recently reached an agreement with Cantor Equity Partners I to terminate the business combination agreement both sides had previously signed. The planned path to go public via this SPAC and transition into a publicly traded Bitcoin reserves company has now been halted. The arrangement was once seen as an important attempt to bring institutionalized Bitcoin allocation capabilities to the public markets; now, with negotiations between the two parties, it has been formally wrapped up.

Regarding the background, BSTR and Cantor Equity Partners I signed a business combination agreement on July 16, 2025. The goal was to use the SPAC route to complete a public listing, with Bitcoin reserves and related treasury strategies as the core business positioning. Public information shows the project received support from Adam Back, and the market at one point interpreted it as one of the samples extending the institutional Bitcoin narrative into the U.S. public markets. Meanwhile, industry discussions around structured financing methods such as Bitcoin treasury tools, convertible bonds, and preferred shares have also been quite active, which is why BSTR’s path to listing drew attention.

On the core facts, both sides have agreed to terminate the merger agreement. BSTR said that Bitcoin and publicly listed Bitcoin treasury-type tools are still facing significant pricing pressure. A mismatch in the market environment has limited the effective use of leverage strategies tools such as convertible bonds and perpetual preferred shares. Even so, the company still believes that as the market gradually stabilizes, opportunities for Bitcoin allocations and related leveraged investments in the public markets may reappear. BSTR co-founder and CEO Adam Back said Cantor Equity Partners I and the Cantor team have always been excellent partners, and this termination is a decision made jointly by both sides. Even in the current environment, the company still sees a substantial demand in the market for Bitcoin returns, and has continued to build the relevant capabilities over the past year. BSTR co-founder and Chief Investment Officer Sean Bill said the team has assembled professionals in institutional investing and Bitcoin protocol, and will continue to design, build, and expand institution-level strategies aimed at Bitcoin returns and building the Bitcoin capital markets. Other reports indicate that BSTR Holdings must pay Cantor Equity Partners I $10 million by September 19 and $5 million by December 1, or otherwise it may be required to have Blockstream Capital Partners make the payments on its behalf.

Breaking down the logic, the termination decision appears to be more of a realignment of financing and valuation terms than a straightforward rejection of the Bitcoin treasury model itself. If publicly listed Bitcoin treasury tools continue to face pressure, it would directly compress the pricing space and investor acceptance for instruments such as convertible bonds and preferred shares, thereby weakening the capital structure support needed for a SPAC merger. By choosing to terminate together, the parties indicate that under the given terms, the cost-benefit of proceeding with the listing is no longer a match. At the same time, BSTR emphasized it will continue to pursue its Bitcoin treasury business, meaning that business capability building and the listing pathway are two separable tracks. Exiting the current public listing arrangement in the short term does not mean exiting related asset and strategy deployments.

As for the impact path on the crypto market, it mainly shows up on expectations and the structure level. First, the pace at which institutions quickly form a narrative of “a Bitcoin reserves public company” through SPACs may slow down, making the market more sensitive to valuation discounts and financing difficulty for similar merger listings. Second, attention in the Bitcoin treasury segment may shift from “getting listed as soon as possible” to “whether it can obtain sustainable capital instruments and reasonable pricing in the public markets.” Third, for retail investors, events of this kind more often affect risk appetite and topic heat rather than directly changing the fundamentals of the Bitcoin network. What truly needs monitoring is whether there will be subsequent alternative listing routes, private financing arrangements, and how the public-market Bitcoin-related equity instruments’ premium/discount may correct.

Editor’s view and observations: This termination provides a calm, case-study sample— even with industry-known supporters and a clear Bitcoin treasury positioning, the public-market path still heavily depends on the pricing environment and whether structured financing is feasible. BSTR chose to keep pushing the business while ending the current SPAC merger, which is a pragmatic adjustment under constraints. What is worth tracking going forward is whether its institutional strategy can continue to be implemented under a non-listed framework, and the time window in which similar Bitcoin treasury entities may regain space for capital instruments in the public markets, rather than whether a single transaction succeeds or fails. From a factual standpoint, the merger has been terminated, the payment milestones and statements by both parties are already clear. As to when the market stabilizes and when leverage tools may become effective again, those remain forward-looking judgments that should be distinguished from later disclosures.

content:
BSTR终止与Cantor SPAC合并 比特币财库上市中止

由Adam Back支持的比特币财库公司BSTR Holdings，近日与Cantor Equity Partners I达成一致，终止双方此前签署的业务合并协议，原计划通过该SPAC上市并转型为公开市场比特币储备公司的路径就此中止。这一安排曾被视为将机构化比特币配置能力带入公开市场的重要尝试，如今在双方协商下正式收官。

事件背景方面，BSTR与Cantor Equity Partners I于2025年7月16日签署业务合并协议，目标是借助SPAC通道完成上市，并以比特币储备与相关财库策略作为核心业务定位。公开信息显示，该项目获得Adam Back方面支持，市场一度将其解读为比特币机构化叙事向美股公开市场延伸的样本之一。与此同时，行业内围绕比特币财库工具、可转债及优先股等结构化融资手段的讨论也较为活跃，BSTR的上市路径因此受到关注。

核心事实方面，双方已协商一致终止合并协议。BSTR方面表示，比特币及公开上市的比特币财库类工具当前仍面临较大定价压力，市场环境错位限制了可转债、永续优先股等杠杆策略工具的有效运用。尽管如此，公司仍相信随着市场逐步企稳，公开市场中的比特币配置与相关杠杆投资机会有望再现。BSTR联合创始人兼首席执行官Adam Back称，Cantor Equity Partners I与Cantor团队始终是出色的合作伙伴，此次终止系双方共同决定；即便在当前环境下，公司仍看到市场对比特币回报存在可观需求，并已在过去一年持续打造相应能力。BSTR联合创始人兼首席投资官Sean Bill则表示，团队已汇聚机构投资与比特币协议领域专业人才，将继续设计、构建并扩展面向比特币回报及比特币资本市场建设的机构级策略。另有报道指出，BSTR Holdings需在9月19日前向Cantor Equity Partners I支付1000万美元，并在12月1日前支付500万美元，否则可能要求Blockstream Capital Partners代为支付。

从逻辑拆解看，终止决定更接近对融资与估值条件的现实校准，而非单纯否定比特币财库模式本身。公开上市比特币财库工具若持续承压，会直接压缩可转债、优先股等工具的定价空间与投资者接受度，进而削弱SPAC合并所需的资本结构支撑。双方选择共同终止，说明在既定条款下推进上市的成本收益已难匹配；与此同时，BSTR强调仍将推进比特币财库业务，意味着业务能力建设与上市通道是两条可拆分的路径，短期退出公开上市安排，并不等同于退出相关资产与策略布局。

对加密市场的影响路径，主要体现在预期与结构层面。其一，机构通过SPAC快速形成“比特币储备上市公司”的叙事节奏可能放缓，市场对同类并购上市的估值折扣与融资难度会更加敏感。其二，比特币财库赛道的关注点或从“尽快上市”转向“能否在公开市场获得可持续的资本工具与合理定价”。其三，对普通投资者而言，这类事件更多影响风险偏好与主题热度，而非直接改变比特币网络基本面；真正需要观察的是后续是否还有替代上市路径、私募融资安排，以及公开市场比特币相关股权工具的折溢价修复情况。

编辑判断与观察：此次终止提供了一个冷静样本——即便具备行业知名支持者与明确比特币财库定位，公开市场路径仍高度依赖定价环境与结构化融资可行性。BSTR选择保留业务推进、同时结束当前SPAC合并，属于在约束条件下的务实调整。后续更值得跟踪的是其机构策略能否在非上市框架下持续落地，以及同类比特币财库主体在公开市场重新获得资本工具空间的时间窗口，而非单次交易成败本身。事实层面，合并已终止、付款节点与双方表态已明确；关于市场何时企稳、杠杆工具何时重新有效，仍属前瞻判断，需与后续披露区分看待。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Having seen the “native issuance” that @Dusk_Foundation  has been aggressively promoting, I decided to take off the rose-colored glasses and take a look at the ledgers. They believe that the RWA on the market today are nothing but fake demand—traditional assets are merely wrapped in a blockchain skin, while real settlement still goes on inside the old systems. Dusk’s ambitions are far from small: it wants to hard-code dividends, KYC checks, and trading restrictions directly into the underlying protocol, effectively upending the current structure of capital operations. #dusk

But when I dug into the Digital Euro EURQ (led by Quantoz), which serves as the settlement core, I found the on-chain data to be rather underwhelming. This thing is essentially casting a wide net—it runs on Ethereum, Algorand, Polygon, XRPL, and Stellar. After reviewing Quantoz’s publicly available reports, it’s clear that the real value backing EURQ hasn’t formed any obvious concentration on Dusk. A chain that claims to be tailor-made for asset issuance couldn’t even intercept the bulk of the funds that drive its featured pricing currency—pretty awkward, to say the least. $DUSK

Looking at Dusk’s collaboration with the Dutch MTF institution NPEX, the reality is even more of a thunderclap with little rain. NPEX holds 102 projects and a 196M euro capital pool, but take a look at DuskEVM—its current DeFi TVL hasn’t even reached the “passing” mark of a million dollars. If there really were a massive amount of assets being natively issued on-chain, surely there would be some sign of activity in liquidity pools. What we see instead is that while the XSC standard can get whitelist and dividend distribution working, this KYC system by Citadel still relies on traditional off-chain service providers for endorsement. Bottom line: it’s still a transitional product of “paperwork handled off-chain, run-of-the-mill on-chain.” It’s still far from a fully self-sufficient on-chain capital ecosystem.

As for the officially promoted T+0—technically, it does indeed outclass the traditional finance’s T+2. But as long as the key to deposits and withdrawals is controlled by Quantoz’s EMI license, and trading matching still depends on NPEX, then Dusk can at most be viewed as a privacy-protected posting channel; it can’t be considered an independent, self-driven new market.

To sum up: Dusk’s ZK technology and MiCA compliance credentials are certainly solid, but “native issuance” is still only a marketing phrase for now. Going forward, one thing I’ll be watching closely is this: when will EURQ’s share of funds on the Dusk network break away from the other chains and become clearly dominant on its own? If you can’t kick the addiction to traditional custodians’ “pacifiers,” then those fancy contract standards are all hollow. #eth $ETH

translatedData.content:
#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Recently, I took a close look at @Dusk_Foundation ’s frequently mentioned “native issuance” and found that the gap between vision and reality is not small. They complain that today’s RWA is nothing more than putting a digital shell over traditional assets, with core business still entirely off-chain. Dusk’s ambition is to hard-code KYC, trading rules, and dividend mechanisms directly into the protocol layer, trying to fundamentally reshape the financial structure. #dusk

However, I checked the deployment of EURQ, the core settlement asset in its ecosystem. This digital euro issued by Quantoz actually spans multiple chains, including Ethereum, Algorand, Polygon, XRPL, and even Stellar. Although Dusk is also one of the partners, in the publicly available reserve reports, the funds backing EURQ have not flowed toward Dusk at all. If a chain that loudly claims to be built for native assets cannot even retain the most critical settlement tool, where is its moat? $DUSK

What is even more puzzling is the progress on the NPEX side. This Dutch MTF holds a massive scale of 102 financing deals and 196M euros, but in contrast, DuskEVM’s current DeFi TVL cannot even reach 1 million dollars. If there really were huge amounts of securities being natively issued on-chain, there should at least be some trace of a liquidity pool. The reality is that even though the XSC contract supports whitelisting and rollback, Citadel’s identity verification still cannot bypass offline service providers. The so-called “native” is at best a hybrid of “on-chain privacy + off-chain review.”

Even if T+0 instant settlement is technically achievable, as long as deposits and withdrawals depend on Quantoz’s EMI license and trade matching still has to go through NPEX, Dusk is nothing more than a clearing channel with a privacy halo. Its ZK technology and MiCA compliance credentials are indeed strong, but “native issuance” is, at this stage, still just a narrative. My core focus going forward is only one thing: can EURQ’s circulation on Dusk truly explode, and can the chain really grow a genuine securities scale that breaks away from traditional custody? #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation I was digging through some code recently and noticed that @Dusk fixed a particularly sneaky low-level “quirk.” In their G1/G2 curve data storage, there’s a flag originally set up to determine whether something is the point at infinity. Under normal logic, it’s a multiple-choice situation: either set it to 0 (standard) or 1 (special). But early systems somehow skipped one security check—so even if you insert a meaningless value like “2,” the system still swallows it. This creates a third possibility out of thin air, and it directly puts a crack in a carefully designed cryptographic foundation.

When I see something like this, I’m actually even more afraid. If the system simply crashes completely, everyone can quickly follow the trail back to the source. The most disgusting scenario is the kind where damage is done quietly: because different compilation environments have different levels of leniency, the testnet might encounter this “2” and immediately error out, blocking it, while the mainnet official version might relax some validations and let corrupted data keep running. The same data, two different outcomes across two environments—that’s effectively planting a mine. At that point, the main chain may still be producing blocks, but surrounding nodes, wallets, or query plugins could already be down. You think nobody is trading, but it’s the infrastructure itself that’s gone off the rails.

This really leaves me with a deep impression: when it comes to finding security vulnerabilities, you really can’t just obsess over the high-level equations in the whitepaper. How exactly does data reading get implemented in practice? When faced with out-of-bounds parameters, can the system cut it off immediately? Are the execution steps of dev and production versions absolutely consistent? These engineering details are the real moat. Even if a single byte of capacity is small, if you can just fill it arbitrarily, in business logic it becomes a ticking time bomb.

Back to the secondary market: patching such fine-grained issues won’t immediately spur retail holders for $DUSK  to chase the rally, and the token price is unlikely to jump straight up just because a low-level fix was applied. But for large players, what they watch is exactly this kind of “engineering deployment risk,” which directly determines how much discount institutions apply to the project in their minds.

So far, Dusk has already force-locked the core components to accept only 0 and 1, which is a positive signal. As for when the new code will be fully implemented on mainnet, we’ll need to keep observing. After all, when building financial infrastructure, there’s no room for any specks of dust. #eth $ETH

遇到这种事，我反而更怕。如果系统直接全面崩溃，大家立马就能顺藤摸瓜找到源头。最恶心的是那种“闷声搞破坏”的情况：由于不同编译环境的宽容度不一样，测试网碰见这个“2”可能直接报错拦截，但主网正式版如果放宽了某些校验，就会任由错乱的数据继续跑。同一份数据，两套环境跑出两个结局，这无疑是在埋雷。这时候，主链也许还在出块，但周边的节点、钱包或者查询插件可能早就宕机了。你以为是没人交易了，其实是基础设施自己岔道了。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  This time @Dusk_Foundation  the official code repository fixed a small flaw that made me break out in a cold sweat. In the module where they store G1/G2 elliptic curve data, there’s a dedicated parameter used to confirm whether the point is the “point at infinity.” If you know the subject, you’d know this is originally a strict either-or situation: put 0 for normal coordinates, and put 1 for the special zero point. But the old version program somehow didn’t enforce the strict check—if you just inject any number (say, toss in a “2”), the system still treats it as a normal file and happily swallows it.

Compared to a network that outright collapses, I’m actually more afraid of this kind of “silent corruption.” It’s easier to handle when nodes all go down, because then you can hunt for the cause. What’s most tormenting, though, is that the same malformed data can receive totally different treatment under different runtime environments. For example, the testnet is strict and will immediately report an error and block it; but on the mainnet, for efficiency, they disabled some validations and let this “2” slip through. That’s a problem: the same document, two programs produce completely opposite conclusions. The result is that the underlying chain might still be running, but the peripheral wallet frontend, proving components, or block-checking tools are completely confused—then they hang on the spot.

You think no one is interacting, but really it’s the infrastructure components themselves that generate a state mismatch.

This also highlights, indirectly, that code auditing must not only look at how pretty the formulas are in the whitepaper. How the input side receives parameters, at which checkpoint out-of-spec values are rejected, and whether the tolerance rates match between development and production—these are all the life-or-death gates that financial-grade networks must守住. No matter how generous the memory is, if what you feed in doesn’t conform to business logic, it’s poison.

To be frank, filling in such an obscure low-level trap and expecting it to immediately lead to a big wave of short-term retail buying pressure, or to massively pump the $DUSK  token price, isn’t realistic. Its core significance, however, is to reduce “engineering implementation risk.” When major institutions evaluate whether a project is worth heavy investment, the security discount they apply is precisely based on how tightly they can control details like this.

Fortunately, the Dusk team has already added strong validation to the BLS core library. From now on, it will be mandatory to accept only 0 and 1. As for when this new rule can be fully deployed to the mainnet, we’ll have to keep tracking it. #eth $ETH

你以为是没人交互了，其实是基建组件自己产生了状态撕裂。

好在Dusk团队已经在BLS核心库里补上了强校验，以后强制规定只认0和1。至于这套新规什么时候能全面部署到主网上，咱们还得持续跟进。#eth $ETH

After this ETH sell-off, Aave’s bad debt risk has come to the forefront: why everyone is focusing on the lending protocol first

ETH has fallen to $2,396.81, and the concentration of large holders’ collateral debt on Aave is too high—so the market has started to worry about a liquidation cascade.

Aave is the largest lending protocol on Ethereum. Its core logic is simple: you deposit collateral to borrow assets, and when prices drop, liquidations occur. The problem is that the debt is highly concentrated—just a few big whales have borrowed a significant portion of the funds in the pool. An analysis by Bitcoinist points out that after this round of volatility, this concentration amplifies the protocol’s bad-debt exposure. Put bluntly, one whale liquidating is not the same order of magnitude as a hundred retail users liquidating. If a big holder’s collateral price drops quickly and liquidations aren’t timely, the gap has to be covered by the bad-debt reserves; if those reserves can’t cover it, depositors are the ones who pay.

In one sentence: the lending pool looks big, but the risk is in the hands of a few big whales—once ETH drops, everyone starts checking whether the firewall is thick enough.

Market impact
- Short term: bearish. ETH is down 1.27% over the past 24 hours, and sentiment was already weak. This news will intensify concerns about a DeFi liquidation spiral. Around $2,396.81, if that level breaks, positions with high collateral ratios could be liquidated in sequence. The resulting selling pressure could then hit ETH spot, creating a negative feedback loop. BTC $76,334.51 also won’t be able to stand apart; DeFi risk often spreads into broader market sentiment.
- Medium term: if bad debt really occurs, regulators and institutions’ trust in DeFi could take a step backward. Conversely, if Aave weathers this volatility, its risk-control data could become an industry benchmark.

My view
In the short term, I’m mostly bearish and would wait. There are no clear signs that ETH at $2,396.81 has stabilized. The support is at $2,396.81; if it breaks, liquidation pressure may be concentrated and released, possibly causing a rapid probe around the $2,396.81 area. For protocols like Aave, the volatility of their protocol tokens can be greater than that of ETH itself. But I don’t think this is a system-wide collapse event. The size of Aave’s bad-debt reserves has been sufficient in past stress tests. The more likely scenario is consolidation and digestion rather than a chain reaction of explosions. The key risk is this: if ETH’s single-day decline exceeds 8%, the concentration issue could shift from “discussion” to “an accident.”

title: مستقبل العملات الرقمية: هل تشهد الأسواق فرصة دخول حقيقية؟
subTitle:
يُظهر سوق الكريبتو نضجاً هيكلياً مقارنةً بالدورات السابقة؛ حيث تحول الاستثمار في الأصول الرقمية من مجرد مضاربة أفراد إلى اعتماد مؤسسي تنظيمي واسع.

المحركات الأساسية لنضج السوق والمستقبل:

التكامل المباشر مع المؤسسات (ETFs & TradFi): شهد السوق تدفقات مستمرة عبر صناديق المؤشرات المتداولة (Spot ETFs) للبيتكوين والإيثريوم، مما خلق "أرضية سيولة" أقوى يشارك فيها كبار المستثمرين التقليديين.
ترميز أصول العالم الحقيقي (RWA): انتقال السندات الحكومية والأسهم والعقارات لتصبح رموزاً رقمية يُدار تداولها على الشبكات اللامركزية عبر تقنيات Layer-2.
التطور التشريعي: صدور أطر تنظيمية أكثر وضوحاً في الولايات المتحدة والاتحاد الأوروبي يوفر حماية أكبر للمستثمرين ويعزز ثقة رؤوس الأموال الضخمة.

هل التصحيح الحالي فرصة شراء؟
شهدت الأسواق فترات تراجع وتجميع حاد بعد القمم التاريخية السابقة (مثل تجاوز البيتكوين حاجز 120 ألف دولار)، مما أعاد تقييم الأصول إلى مستويات جذابة فدخول الأسواق أثناء مراحل الخوف والتجميع غالباً ما يوفر نقطة دخول جيدة مقارنة بالشراء أثناء اندفاع الهوس السعري (FOMO).

أبرز الاستراتيجيات للتعامل مع الفرص الحالية:

استراتيجية متوسط التكلفة الدولارية (DCA): بدلاً من استثمار رأس المال بالكامل دفعة واحدة، يتم تقسيم المبلغ وشراء أجزاء بشكل دوري (أسبوعي أو شهري) لتقليل تأثير التقلبات السعرية اللحظية.
التركيز على الأصول ذات الأساسيات القوية: توزيع المحفظة بحيث تشكل العملات القياسية (Bitcoin وEthereum) الحصة الكبرى، مع تخصيص نسبة مدروسة للشبكات الواعدة (مثل شبكات Layer-2 ومشاريع RWA والذكاء الاصطناعي).
إدارة المخاطر الصارمة: تجنب التداول باستخدام الروافع المالية (Leverage)، مع الاحتفاظ بنسبة من السيولة النقدية $USDC $USDT $BTC {spot}(BTCUSDT){spot}(USDCUSDT)تقتنص الهبوط المباغت إن حدث.

تساعد معرفة أهدافك الاستثمارية ومستوى مخاطرتك في تحديد كيفية بناء محفظة متوازنة ومناسبة لظروفك المالية.

Solana has secured the top spot for tokenized stock DeFi deposits, with $75 million in capital locked on-chain—directly benefiting SOL’s RWA narrative.

So-called tokenized stocks mean packaging US stock shares into on-chain tokens that can be traded and used as collateral in DeFi to earn yield within 24 hours. Funds have been flowing into this sector quickly. Among them, 75% of the deposits—$75 million—are concentrated on the Solana chain, not Ethereum. 三个周期目前是"日线强、短线钝"的劈叉结构。日线收 2422，MA7(2252)/MA25(1988)/MA50(1920) 全被踩在脚下，RSI14 53.4 中性偏上不超买，MACD 站在零轴上方、红柱没塌——中期多头结构完好的前提下，这波从 1847 拉到 2549 的幅度（约 +38%）还没走坏。但短周期已经在预警：4h 收 2423，RSI14 干到 69.5 贴着 70 上沿，MA7(2418) 跟 MA25(2356) 开始黏合，2549 那根上影说明上方抛压实打实；1h 更弱，收 2423 被 MA50(2430) 压在头上下不来，RSI14 67.2 从高位回吐，近 20 根高低点 2355–2444 锁在一个窄箱里磨。价在 1h 均线下方、日线均线上方，标准的"大涨后高位洗盘"架子，不是转空。

关键位划死：上方 2549 是这轮反弹高点第一坎，摸了就出上影，拿下才谈往 2700 走；再上 2800 是前高密集成交区。下方 2400 整数口是多空第一道防线，回踩不破就认强势整理；2355（今天低点）是短线命门，真跌破前面追高盘就松；2250 附近（日 MA7）是更强支撑叠区，不破结构还在。

💧 衍生品与链上
资金费率 0.0001（8h，约日化 +0.03%），踩在币安永续费率上限，多头付费持多但没到疯狂，情绪偏热不过热。未平仓 2,399,321 ETH（约 58 亿 USDT），跟昨天的 240 万基本持平——价横 OI 不动，说明多空都没在这个位置大砍，是换手不是出逃。散户账户多空比 2.5587（多头占 71.9%），一边倒看多；top trader 持仓多空比 1.726（多头占 63.3%），大户净多但没散户那么极端。这种"散户扎堆多、聪明钱温和多"的组合，上涨时爽、一插针就容易被猎。ETH/BTC 0.03144 微跌，相对强度暂时落后大饼。Fear&Greed 66（Greed，和昨天持平），贪婪还在高位没退潮。质押/ETF 净流精确值公开通道拉不到不瞎编，但 OI 持平+费率封顶这两个信号能对上"资金没撤、杠杆偏热"的判断。

📰 消息面
实时新闻通道今晚走不通（数据源限频/需付费订阅，拉不到 ETH 单条硬催化），不编事件。技术+衍生品在"缩量横盘+费率封顶+OI 持平+散户扎堆多"里，更像反弹后的高位换手，不是趋势反转。宏观风险情绪偏暖，FNG 66 能对上。

👉 我的看法
短线读成"反弹后高位缩量洗盘"的震荡局，不是转空。日线多头结构完好、OI 没撤，2400 不破就是强势整理，等 1h 重新站回 MA50(2430) 且 RSI 收回 60 上方，才认回踩结束重启短多。没仓别在 2422 急着接：要么等 2400 企稳轻仓上车，要么等放量站回 2549 不回头认延续。有仓止损挂 2355（今天低点）下方，OI 58 亿不低、插针振幅仍狠。中线偏多：日线稳站 2250 且 RSI 守 50 上方，才认中期延续往 2700–2800；2250 不破仍是偏强区间。仓位控小，这种反弹后的回踩比平时更考验拿单心态。

The things that bring truly high returns are often not about catching a single opportunity.

Many people are always searching for the next breakout: 

the next coin that will skyrocket, 
the next bull market, 
the next sudden chance to turn things around.

But what truly changes a person’s long-term outcome is usually not that you bet right once,

but that you find something you can compound over time,
then keep repeating it.

Learn a little more every day, and your cognition compounds;
keep producing consistently, and your influence compounds;
fulfill your commitments again and again, and your credibility compounds;
accumulate principal over the long term, and your capital compounds;
keep optimizing your system, and your capabilities compound as well.

In the beginning,
all of this is very slow.
So slow that you may even start to wonder if it’s even useful.

And most people fall exactly here:

seeing no results, they change direction;
if they can’t make quick money, they chase the hot spots;
a few months of sticking with it makes them feel like they’ve already persisted for a long time.

But the most brutal—and fair—thing about compounding is this:

in the early stage, it rewards patience;
in the later stage, it rewards time.

The truly high-return things are not about how much smarter you are than others,
or how many opportunities you managed to catch.

It’s about finding something with the right direction—something you can compound—and then sticking with it.

Persist until most people lose patience;
persist until peers start to drop out;
persist until time stands on your side.

In the end, you’ll find that the place where others quit is often where compounding truly begins.

# I tell you the truth behind my worst trade: $BTC 
After the drop, I used AI as a “confirmation-bias printer” and dug my own grave

I used AI to review 127 trades, and the most painful conclusion isn’t that my win rate was low.
What really ate my profits was that extra click every time I felt, “This time it’s different.”

I exported three months of execution records and, trade by trade, filled in four columns: entry rationale, whether I added on the fly, whether the stop-loss was moved, and my emotional state before placing the order. Then I had AI only categorize—not predict price moves. The results were ugly: 83 trades executed according to the original plan had a normal profit/loss distribution; but the 44 trades where I changed the plan on the spot contributed nearly 70% of the drawdown.

The most typical case was after $BTC  quickly dipped and then rebounded. I originally planned only to observe. When I saw three consecutive short-term bullish candles, I had the model re-explain the move. The first answer was too cautious, so I changed three sets of prompts until it produced a more optimistic justification before I placed the trade. That wasn’t the AI’s judgment—it was me using AI as a “confirmation-bias printer.”

Later, I changed my process: before placing an order, I first wrote one sentence—“What fact appeared that proves I was wrong?” The model was only allowed to check for logical loopholes; it couldn’t give buy/sell conclusions. Also, for the same trade, you’re not allowed to keep asking about the direction repeatedly. Same story for $ETH —no matter how “hot” the narrative sounds, first check whether I secretly changed the rules. This tweak didn’t help me find more opportunities, but it clearly reduced impulsive actions and wasted trading fees.

The best thing AI can do is be a cold, ruthless auditor: tally where you chase highs in certain market conditions, when you love to hold losers, and which “reasons” are just post-hoc packaging. It shouldn’t be the one taking the risk for you—and it definitely shouldn’t be the one enduring your losses. The better a model is at convincing you, the more you need to guard against the fact that it only picks the answers you want to hear.

#AI交易 #交易复盘 #BTC #ETH

# 我把最惨的一笔交易的真相告诉你：$BTC 下跌后，我拿 AI 当“确认偏误打印机”坑了自己

我用 AI 复盘了 127 笔交易，最扎心的结论不是胜率低。
真正吞掉收益的，是我每次觉得“这次不一样”时多按的那一下。

我把三个月的成交记录导出来，逐笔补了四列：进场理由、是否临时加仓、止损有没有移动、下单前情绪。再让 AI 只做归类，不预测涨跌。结果很难看：按原计划执行的 83 笔，盈亏分布正常；临时改计划的 44 笔，却贡献了接近七成的回撤。

最典型的一次是 $BTC 快速下探后反弹。我原本只准备观察，看到连续三根短周期阳线，就让模型重新解释走势。第一次回答偏谨慎，我换了三个提示词，直到它给出更乐观的论证才下单。那不是 AI 判断，是我拿 AI 当“确认偏误打印机”。

后来我改了流程：下单前先写一句“什么事实出现，证明我错了”；模型只能检查逻辑漏洞，不能给买卖结论；同一笔交易禁止反复追问方向。对 $ETH 也一样，无论叙事多热，先看自己有没有偷偷改规则。这个小改动没有让我抓到更多机会，却明显减少了冲动操作和无效手续费。

AI 最适合做的是冷冰冰的审计员：统计你在哪类行情追高、什么时候爱扛单、哪种理由只是事后包装。它不该替你承担风险，更不会替你承受亏损。模型越会说服人，越要防着自己只挑爱听的答案。

#AI交易 #交易复盘 #BTC #ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Recently, in the crypto circle, a lot of people have been talking about what’s going on with DuskEVM’s mainnet. The public’s first instinct is basically: “Dusk has added another ‘EVM-compatible’ new member to the family.” To be honest, I started out thinking along the same lines too. But to really get to the bottom of it, I went through its underlying documentation in depth, and then I realized everyone’s subconscious assumptions were completely off.

According to the official whitepaper’s rigorous definition, DuskEVM isn’t, in the first place, a standalone, fully-fledged public chain. It doesn’t handle accounting; it’s simply an “execution environment” built on top of OP Stack.

In simple terms, it’s not on equal footing with the underlying DuskDS. Instead, it’s a classic “parent-child nested” relationship. All smart contracts running on it, after computing results, package everything and send it back to DuskDS for final confirmation and data storage (DA). This point is made very clearly in a KuCoin research report: the OP Stack scaling approach you usually see is like enjoying shade under the big tree—ultimately, settlement still happens on Ethereum. But DuskEVM is more particular about where it belongs; its “root” is firmly embedded in its own parent, DuskDS.

However, in @Dusk_Foundation ’s day-to-day public statements to the outside world, it’s hard to directly feel this strong binding. The team’s consistent messaging is to push “three-layer modularization”: DuskDS handles settlement, DuskEVM runs execution, and DuskVM handles privacy. This set of talking points is very misleading—it gives people the illusion that they’re moving forward in sync by building three major projects at once.

What fatal consequences can this kind of cognitive bias lead to? The most direct one is that it “traps” the developers who come to build the ecosystem. Many programmers, if they treat it like a standard independent L2 to estimate gas fees, often focus only on the execution-layer overhead, while missing the other friction cost of “sending the data back to the underlying layer for attestation/storage.” Once you’ve written the code halfway and suddenly realize that the on-chain overhead doesn’t match your expectations—only to find that the transaction fees are way higher than estimated—this ecosystem will be difficult to advance sustainably.

After thinking it through all the way, my final recap is this: Dusk embracing modularization is absolutely the right direction. But when we’re doing investment research and evaluation, we must not imagine DuskEVM as a new chain that can scale infinitely. It’s merely a computational wrapper built around the architecture of the original mainnet.#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation 最近圈里不少人在传 DuskEVM 上主网的事，大众的第一直觉基本都是：Dusk 家族又添了一位“EVM兼容”的新成员。老实说，我刚开始也是顺着这个逻辑去理解的。但为了摸清底细，我专门去死磕了一遍它的底层文档，才发现大伙儿的潜意识全想岔了。

根据官方白皮书里的严谨界定：DuskEVM 压根不是一条能够独当一面的公链。它不负责记账，纯粹就是一个基于 OP Stack 搭出来的“执行空间”。

简单来说，它跟底层的 DuskDS 并非平起平坐的平行线，而是典型的“母子嵌套”关系。所有在上面跑的智能合约，算完之后的结果，全得打包扔回 DuskDS 去做最终确认和数据存储（DA）。这一点 KuCoin 的研报点得非常透彻：咱们平时见到的 OP Stack 扩容方案，大树底下好乘凉，最后都去以太坊上做结算；但 DuskEVM 比较认生，它的“根”死死扎在了自家亲爹 DuskDS 上。

不过，你在 @Dusk_Foundation 的日常对外发声里，很难直接感受到这种强绑定。现在团队的统一话术是主推“三层模块化”：DuskDS 管结算，DuskEVM 跑执行，DuskVM 弄隐私。这套话术非常有迷惑性，给人一种齐头并进做三个大项目的错觉。

这种认知上的偏差会带来什么致命后果？最直接的就是把来建生态的开发者给“坑”了。很多程序员如果把它当成常规的独立 L2 去算 Gas 费，往往只盯着执行层那点开销，却漏掉了“把数据传回底层做存证”的另一笔摩擦损耗。一旦代码敲到一半，突然发现链上磨损对不上号，手续费比预估的高出一大截，这生态就很难长远推进了。

盘到最后，我的复盘结论是：Dusk 拥抱模块化这条路走得很对。但我们在做投研评估时，千万别把 DuskEVM 幻想成一条能无限扩展的新链，它无非是套在原主网架构上的一个计算外壳。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Recently, ever since the mainnet has landed, there’s been a lot of talk in the circle about DuskEVM. Most people’s first impression is: Dusk has launched a brand-new network that’s compatible with the EVM. I initially thought the same—until I went digging through the underlying technical whitepaper and realized everyone had gotten it wrong.

By the official, hardcore definition, DuskEVM doesn’t even meet the criteria for an “independent blockchain.” It doesn’t have its own ledger. In essence, it’s a “compute workshop” cobbled together with OP Stack.

Whatever you do, don’t confuse it with DuskDS as if they were parallel twin stars. Their real relationship is an absolute “master–slave binding.” Yes, all smart contracts do run at the EVM layer—but once the transactions are executed, the resulting transaction data must be reported to DuskDS without alteration so DuskDS can finalize the proof-of-record on-chain.

KuCoin, in a research report, put it bluntly: most OP Stack plans treat Ethereum as their backstop, but it locks the settlement step firmly into its own mainnet.

What’s interesting is that if you dig into the tweets from @Dusk_Foundation , you’ll find the team isn’t particularly fond of emphasizing this dependency. Their current favorite story is “three-level modularization”: DuskDS handles settlement, DuskVM handles privacy, and DuskEVM provides applications. If you isolate these three concepts, it’s easy for outsiders to mistakenly think they’re building three independent highways that each go their own way.

The most damaging part of this information asymmetry is that it misleads the project team. If you’re a developer and you truly treat it like a standard Layer 2 for budgeting, you’ll very likely fall into a trap. Because besides the superficial execution fees, you also have to pay an additional “toll” to push the data back into DuskDS. If you only realize midway that the interaction costs are seriously overshooting expectations, the subsequent expansion of the ecosystem will absolutely grind to a halt.

In short: Dusk’s modular route is fine, but we must not imagine DuskEVM as a new blockchain that can grow infinitely and become a giant. In the end, it’s only an execution shell layered on top of an existing system. Once you’ve sorted out this core logic, you can judge its future ceiling without making absurd misjudgments.#eth $ETH

Bitcoin surges more than 23% in a single week, recording its largest weekly gain in more than three years

In recent days, the cryptocurrency market has seen a relatively fast-paced rebound. According to media reports, Bitcoin rose for five consecutive trading days and stood above $78,000 on Friday. The weekly cumulative gain exceeded 23%, marking the largest one-week rise since March 2023. The market has since discussed whether Bitcoin is entering a technical bull market. In the same period, Ethereum broke above $2,500, with major assets generally strengthening in tandem—an indication that the move is not isolated to a single asset.

First, it’s important to clarify: the above price levels and percentage gains are based on after-the-fact summarization of that week’s trading, and are reports of what has already happened, not a real-time description of the current order book.

The core facts can be summarized in three points. First, Bitcoin completed a five-day winning streak and closed the week with a weekly gain of more than 20%, with the timing reaching back to since March 2023. Second, on Friday, the price touched and held above the $78,000 level, making its weekly performance especially striking. Third, the rally has not been driven solely by spot buying; the reports indicate that nearly 190,000 people were liquidated across the global crypto market, with total liquidation amounts of about $1.535 billion. Among this, short positions accounted for roughly $1.236 billion of liquidations, forcing shorts to exit and providing a significant boost to the upward move. Ethereum’s breakout above $2,500 suggests that, at least at the level of major coins, the strength in this round has some degree of synchronicity.

Breaking down the logic, a weekly gain of over 23% typically reflects the combined effect of three forces: trend-following shorts stopping out or being liquidated at key levels, short-term capital chasing momentum, and the market repricing the question of whether a trend reversal is underway. The liquidation amount for shorts is clearly higher than that for longs. This implies that the previously crowded short structure was cleared out in a rapid price advance, creating a short-term positive feedback loop—“rising prices trigger liquidations, and liquidations further propel prices higher.” As for a “technical bull market,” it generally describes a structural change after the rebound from a phase low reaches a specific threshold. It reflects the pace of chart stabilization and drawdown repair, and does not automatically mean that macro liquidity, the regulatory environment, or long-term fundamentals have fully strengthened. Extending the “technical” definition directly into confirmation of medium- to long-term trends can easily blur time horizons.

To understand the impact on the crypto market, it’s helpful to think in terms of mechanisms rather than slogans. First, Bitcoin’s strength often improves overall risk appetite first, and then determines whether liquidity spills over to other assets; if it remains limited to Bitcoin alone, market breadth is still likely to be limited. Second, after large-scale short liquidations, leverage crowding declines, and the short-term volatility “center” may rise, but if subsequent spot and medium-to-long-term capital fail to step in consistently, pullbacks after a spike will also occur more quickly. Third, synchronized strength in major assets such as Ethereum helps reduce the fragility of “only a single asset is strong,” making the rebound more like a repair of risk appetite rather than a mere squeeze.

The above pathways are mechanism-based reasoning based on already disclosed liquidation events and price behavior. They discuss transmission channels, not assertions about the direction of the next stage.

From an editorial perspective, this week’s significance lies in using a sufficiently large weekly gain to break the market’s expectation of weakness or ongoing range-bound trading, forcing it to reassess the short-term trend. However, a single-week surge often also raises volatility. Going forward, what should be observed more closely is the quality of follow-through during pullbacks, whether trading is healthy, and whether the macro and policy environment can provide continued support. A more prudent framing is to view this rally as a strong rebound driven by the resonance between leverage unwinds and sentiment repair. Whether it evolves into an uptrend over a longer time horizon still requires more evidence from both the capital flow side and fundamentals; it should not be replaced by a single technical label.

content:
比特币单周涨超23%创三年多最大周涨幅

近期加密货币市场出现一轮节奏较快的反弹。据媒体报道，比特币连续五个交易日上涨，并在周五站上78000美元；当周累计涨幅超过23%，被指为2023年3月以来最大的单周涨幅，市场也据此讨论其是否进入技术性牛市。同期以太坊升破2500美元，主流资产同步走强的特征较为明显。需要先明确：上述价位与涨幅均来自对该周行情的事后归纳，属于已发生事实的报道口径，而非对当下盘口的实时描述。

核心事实可以概括为三点。第一，比特币完成连涨五日，并以超过两成的周涨幅收官，时间对照点落在2023年3月以来。第二，价格在周五触及并站上78000美元关口，使周线级别表现格外醒目。第三，行情升温并非孤立的现货买盘现象，报道称全球加密市场近19万人遭到爆仓，爆仓总金额约15.35亿美元，其中空单爆仓约12.36亿美元，空头被迫离场对上行形成显著助推。以太坊突破2500美元，则说明本轮强度至少在主流币层面具有一定同步性。

从逻辑上拆解，单周逾23%的涨幅通常对应三股力量叠加：趋势空头在关键位置止损或爆仓、短线资金追逐动量、以及市场对“是否转势”的重新定价。空头爆仓金额明显高于多头，意味着此前拥挤的空头结构在价格快速上移后被集中清理，容易出现“上涨引发清算、清算再推动上涨”的短期正反馈。所谓技术性牛市，多是对价格自阶段低点回升幅度达到特定阈值后的结构描述，它反映的是图表与回撤修复进度，并不自动等于宏观流动性、监管环境或长期基本面已全面转强。把技术定义直接延伸为中长期趋势确认，容易混淆时间尺度。

对加密市场的影响路径，可从结构而非口号理解。其一，比特币的强势往往先改善整体风险偏好，再决定流动性是否向其他资产外溢；若仅停留在比特币单边，市场广度仍然有限。其二，大规模空头清算后，杠杆拥挤度下降，短线波动中枢可能上移，但若后续缺乏持续的现货与中长期资金承接，冲高后的回撤同样会更快。其三，以太坊等主流品种同步走强，有助于降低“只有单一资产强势”的脆弱性，使反弹更像风险偏好修复，而非单纯逼空。以上路径是基于已披露清算与价格行为的机制推演，属于对传导方式的讨论，不是对下一阶段方向的断言。

编辑判断上，本周意义在于用足够大的周涨幅打断了偏弱或震荡的惯性预期，迫使市场重新评估短期趋势。但单周暴涨也往往抬升波动率，后续更应观察回撤时的承接质量、成交是否健康，以及宏观与政策环境能否提供延续性支撑。更稳妥的定位，是把此轮行情理解为杠杆出清与情绪修复共振下的强势反弹；它是否演化为更长时间维度的上升趋势，仍需更多资金面与基本面证据验证，而不宜被单一技术标签所替代。

Anthropic ускоряет IPO; expected fundraising amount could exceed SpaceX’s record

AI company Anthropic is accelerating its push toward an initial public offering (IPO). According to media reports citing people familiar with the matter, the company expects its IPO fundraising to match or even surpass the historical scale set by SpaceX. SpaceX’s initial fundraising totaled about $75 billion; after including the over-allotment option, it reached roughly $86.2 billion, which is seen as one of the largest IPOs in history. The discussions are still ongoing, and there are variables such as the final size. At this stage, it remains in the preparation and expectation phase rather than a priced, finalized outcome.

On key facts, Anthropic plans to publicly file listing documents as early as the end of this month and has already submitted confidential materials. It is working with underwriting teams at Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan Chase, among other banks, to advance underwriting arrangements. In May of this year, the company completed about $65 billion in financing at a valuation of roughly $96.5 billion, exceeding OpenAI’s then-valuation of around $85.2 billion. On governance, the company is considering introducing a super-voting rights structure to strengthen post-IPO decision-making control for CEO Dario Amodei and the founding team. There are also reports that prior to the IPO it plans to finalize a revolving credit facility with a size higher than a prior target of about $10 billion. Performance shows high growth alongside heavy investment: preliminary second-quarter revenue exceeded $11.5 billion, jumping sharply from about $787 million in the same period last year. By the end of July, the annualized revenue run rate was around $65 billion. The adjusted operating profit for the second quarter is said to have turned positive, but the company is expected to record net losses of about $42 billion in 2025, expanding to nearly five times last year’s roughly $8.3 billion. The company also reached a compute-related agreement with SpaceX; over the next three years, the potential value could reach several tens of billions of dollars. Market participants believe that if it successfully goes public and breaks through existing fundraising thresholds, the size of the U.S. IPO market in 2026 could stand out even more. Its timing is also expected to be earlier than the target window, pointing to around 2027 for OpenAI.

From a logic standpoint, whether an ultra-large IPO can truly materialize depends less on “narrative heat” and more on whether the deal can be simultaneously accepted by the public market in three areas: first, whether revenue surges can sustainably cover capital expenditures on compute for training and inference; second, whether cash flow and financing structures during the high-loss phase are transparent, and thus can be priced; and third, whether arrangements such as super-voting rights can achieve a balance between liquidity and founder control. Its compute partnership with SpaceX links commercial spaceflight capacity, data centers, and spending for training cutting-edge models into a longer, capital-intensive chain—highlighting that the AI race is still fundamentally a competition for compute, energy, and balance sheets. It is important to separate facts from speculation: what has been disclosed includes the financing valuation, revenue and loss magnitudes, underwriting and governance directions, and the progress of confidential submissions. Claims such as “fundraising exceeds SpaceX’s record” or “rewriting the annual IPO ranking” still depend on the final offering size, market absorption capacity, and the pricing window, and therefore fall under forward-looking judgment.

Impact on the crypto market is mostly an indirect path via risk appetite and thematic mapping, rather than a direct mapping of fundamentals. A cluster of large AI companies moving toward public markets may reshape valuation anchors for global growth assets and influence the timing of capital flows between primary and secondary markets. If a “monster” issuer’s offering temporarily diverts risk budgets, it could suppress short-term risk appetite for highly volatile instruments, including crypto assets. If AI capital expenditures are interpreted as long-term productivity gains, optimism could propagate along two lines—liquidity expectations and correlations with technology stocks—into higher-beta assets. Meanwhile, constraints on compute, data centers, and energy may strengthen the “AI infrastructure” narrative and indirectly lift discussion momentum around compute-related applications, on-chain agents, and infrastructure themes. However, such mapping is mostly about sentiment and theme rotation, lacking a rigid cash-flow connection to any single token. Therefore, IPO rumor lines cannot be linearly extrapolated into market signals.

Editor’s take: The current main information thread comes from people familiar with the matter and media reports. The formal S-1 terms, the final fundraising range, equity-structure details, and the listing timing could still change. High revenue growth and expanding losses coexist, suggesting that accelerating commercialization has not removed the cost constraints of model iteration. For practitioners in crypto, what may be more worth tracking is how the AI capital expenditure cycle affects expectations for U.S. dollar liquidity, the correlation of Nasdaq growth stocks, and whether the on-chain AI narrative can move from slogans to verifiable demand—rather than directly equating a single company’s IPO prospects with market-direction signals. Going forward, attention should be paid to disclosures in public filings, the underwriting syndicate and credit arrangements being finalized, and changes to the timeline of peer companies’ listings, to distinguish between expected trades and actual progress.

Anthropic加速IPO 募资规模有望超越SpaceX纪录

人工智能公司Anthropic正加速推进首次公开募股。据媒体援引知情人士的信息，公司预计IPO募资规模有望匹配甚至超过SpaceX创下的历史量级。SpaceX首发募资约750亿美元，计入超额配售后约达862亿美元，被视作史上最大规模IPO之一。相关讨论仍在进行，规模等细节存在变数，目前仍属筹备与预期阶段，而非已经定价落地的结果。

核心事实方面，Anthropic计划最早本月底公开递交上市文件，并已进行机密提交，正与摩根士丹利、高盛、摩根大通等投行推进承销安排。今年5月，公司以约9650亿美元估值完成约650亿美元融资，估值超过OpenAI当时约8520亿美元的水平。治理上，公司考虑引入超级投票权结构，以强化首席执行官Dario Amodei及联合创始人团队在上市后的决策控制；另有报道称，IPO前还计划敲定规模高于此前约100亿美元目标的循环信贷安排。业绩呈现高增长与高投入并存：第二季度初步收入超过115亿美元，同比去年同期约7.87亿美元大幅跃升，截至7月底年化收入运行率约650亿美元；第二季度经调整营业利润据称转正，但2025年净亏损约420亿美元，较上年约83亿美元扩大近五倍。公司还与SpaceX达成算力相关协议，未来三年潜在价值可能达数百亿美元。市场人士认为，若其成功上市并突破既有募资门槛，2026年美国IPO市场募资规模有望更为突出；其节奏亦被预期可能早于目标窗口指向2027年前后的OpenAI。

逻辑拆解上，超大额IPO能否成立，关键不在“叙事热度”，而在三方面能否同时被公开市场接受：一是收入爆发能否持续覆盖训练与推理的算力资本开支；二是高亏损阶段的现金流与融资结构是否透明、可定价；三是超级投票权等安排能否在流动性与创始人控制之间取得平衡。与SpaceX的算力合作，把商业航天运力、数据中心与前沿模型训练支出连成更长的资本密集链条，也说明AI竞赛本质上仍是算力、能源与资产负债表的竞赛。需要把事实与推测分开：已披露的是融资估值、收入与亏损量级、承销与治理方向及机密递交进展；“募资超越SpaceX纪录”“改写年度IPO排名”仍取决于最终发行规模、市场承接力和定价窗口，属于前瞻判断。

对加密市场的影响，更多是风险偏好与主题映射的间接路径，而非直接基本面映射。大型AI公司扎堆走向公开市场，可能重塑全球成长资产的估值锚和一级、二级市场资金节奏：若巨无霸发行阶段性分流风险预算，短线或抑制包括加密资产在内的高波动品种风险偏好；若AI资本开支被解读为长期生产力提升，则可能从流动性预期与科技股相关性两条线，向高Beta资产传导乐观情绪。同时，算力、数据中心与能源约束会强化“AI基础设施”叙事，间接抬升市场对算力相关应用、链上代理与基础设施题材的讨论热度，但这类映射多为情绪与主题轮动，缺少与单一代币现金流的刚性对应，不能把IPO传闻线性外推为行情依据。

编辑判断：当前信息主轴来自知情人士与媒体报道，正式S-1条款、最终募资区间、股权结构细节与上市时点仍可能调整。收入高增与亏损扩大并存，提示商业化加速并未消除模型迭代的成本约束。对加密从业者而言，更值得跟踪的是AI资本开支周期如何影响美元流动性预期、纳斯达克成长股相关性，以及链上AI叙事能否从口号走向可验证需求，而不是把单一公司上市预期直接等同于市场方向信号。后续应关注公开文件披露、承销团与信贷安排落地，以及同业上市时间表变化，以区分预期交易和实质进展。

Before bed I checked again—still the same price.

Paul Tudor Jones has a saying I’ve remembered to this day.

He said that every morning he wakes up assuming every position is wrong.

Defense first, offense second.

For someone who can live thirty years, what they think about is how not to die.

Not how to get rich.

Today, $ETH  is up only 1.11%, with turnover of 849 million.

Looks steady? That’s precisely the part that lets people relax.

Jones would treat those 849 million as an opponent that can flip on you at any moment.

Before holding overnight, ask yourself first: where am I wrong?

Grind it out here tonight—tomorrow it might gap straight up or down.

What he’s afraid of isn’t falling, but believing he’s right.

Waiting and watching. It’s Sunday evening now, not many people are watching the order book. Everyone feels it’s garbage time with no direction.
As a result, BTC got dumped down to 75,546, but now it’s pulled back to 77,488.
With an $1.111 billion trading volume, that’s really not small for a Sunday.
If it could drop to 75,546 and then come back up, it means there’s money underneath still stepping in.
The RSI has recovered from the oversold zone back to 46—not strong, but the direction is pointing upward.
The MACD short-term bullish crossover has just barely started to show.
MA5 is at 76,800, MA20 at 75,900, and the price is trading above both.
Most of the short positions were swept out on the rebound, which is why the bounce is so smooth.
The daily chart isn’t that optimistic, though. The high at 77,766 pressed down all day and wasn’t broken.
There are buyers underneath and sellers overhead, with chop in the middle.
75,546 is today’s panic low, and it’s the most solid support in my eyes.
77,766 is today’s high—before it breaks through, I can’t say a trend reversal has happened.
My own trades: I went long around 76,800, cut half at 77,766, and the remaining position’s stop loss is set at 75,400.
ETH is stronger than BTC today. It pulled back from 2,356 to 2,459, up 1.20%.
Trading volume is 774 million; compared with BTC, ETH’s “buyer support” is stronger.
AAVE is the most impressive: it surged 12.92%. The volume at 39 million isn’t huge, but it was enough to push the price up.
This kind of sudden run-up is most common when liquidity is thin—let’s see tomorrow whether it can hold above 140.
Today’s lesson: On Sundays, big bullish candles and big bearish candles can both be fake. Liquidity is too thin—don’t rush to believe it.
Hold 40% of the position. If 75,546 breaks, then exit.

# I find reasons to place orders every day, and the cost is ridiculously high— in just 31 days, I did 96 “fear of missing out” operations.

My account is up 18%, yet I gave back almost a quarter of it to the market.
It’s not that I got the direction wrong—it’s that in those 31 days I did 96 “fear of missing out” operations.

That month the market was active, and every day I could find reasons to place orders: follow the breakout, catch the pullback, and if it went sideways I’d worry it might suddenly start moving. By month-end when reconciling, the statement showed a positive balance—but when I listed the fees, slippage, and a few quick stop-losses after chasing, the costs were outrageous. Especially on nights when <t-2/> $BTC  started amplifying volatility, I often mistook “lots of movement” as “lots of opportunity.”

I came up with a dumb workaround: group every trade by holding time. Fewer than two hours were 57 trades—almost no contribution to profit overall, yet they ate up most of the fees. What actually made the difference, instead, was a small number of trades where I had the logic written in advance and waited patiently for confirmation. Even more awkward: I kept switching between $BNB  and $ETH , which looked like diversification of risk—but in reality it was just paying for my anxiety over and over.

Later I added three frictions for myself: check candidate opportunities no more than twice a day; the reason for placing an order must be explainable in three sentences; and if the reason is only “it hasn’t gone up yet,” I skip it. During weekly reviews, I no longer just look at profit and loss—I look at how much “each click” costs. This metric is especially brutal because it exposes that kind of trading habit that looks diligent on the surface but is actually random.

It’s normal for a trading platform to want you to be active. But your job isn’t to create trading volume—it’s to decide whether a specific risk is worth taking. Doing fewer trades isn’t automatically superior, and trading more often isn’t automatically professional. The key is whether each trade has an independent, verifiable reason—not coming up with excuses just because the market looks lively.

# 我每天都在找理由下单，结果成本高得离谱，仅 31 天就做了 96 次“怕错过”的操作。

账户盈利 18%，我却把其中近四分之一还给了市场。
不是方向看错，而是 31 天里做了 96 次“怕错过”的操作。

那个月行情活跃，我每天都能找到理由下单：突破要跟，回踩要接，横盘又怕突然启动。月底对账时，账面确实是正的，但把手续费、滑点和几次追涨后的快速止损单独列出来，成本高得离谱。尤其在 $BTC 波动放大的晚上，我常把“波动很多”误认为“机会很多”。

我做了个笨办法：把每笔交易按持仓时间分组。少于两小时的 57 笔，整体几乎没贡献利润，却吃掉了大部分手续费；真正拉开结果的，反而是少数提前写好逻辑、耐心等确认的交易。更尴尬的是，我在 $BNB 和 $ETH 之间频繁切换，看起来像分散风险，本质上只是不断为焦虑付费。

后来我给自己加了三道摩擦：一天最多检查两次候选机会；下单理由必须能用三句话写清；如果理由只有“它还没涨”，直接跳过。每周复盘时，我不再只看盈亏，而是看“每一次点击值多少钱”。这项数据特别残酷，因为它能揭穿那种表面勤奋、实际乱动的交易习惯。

交易平台希望你活跃，这很正常；但你的任务不是贡献成交量，而是判断某次风险是否值得承担。少操作不天然高级，频繁操作也不天然专业。关键是每一笔有没有独立、可验证的理由，而不是行情热闹时给手痒找借口。

Brothers, ETH is now around 2460. In a week it ran from 1868 all the way to 2549—starting with a 30-point move. This rocket has no issues.

First, here’s the conclusion: I recognize the direction, I’m bullish on it. But I won’t chase from this position—I’ll wait for a pullback.

Let’s talk about the money first. Money is the most honest. The spot big orders have stayed consistent for five consecutive window candles—none have dropped. In the past three hours, net inflow hit 12 candles, all red. That’s real gold and white silver flowing in.

What feels best is the fee rate is only 0.01%, and leverage hasn’t really caught fire. This move isn’t imaginary heat—it’s spot orders honestly taking the other side.

But the problem is the order book: the buy side is paper-thin, like a sheet. The buy-sell ratio is barely above 0.1. And sell walls above are pinned down hard—there are orders stacked tightly overhead.

Also look at positioning: retail accounts are about 70% long, but the whales’ positions have actually shrunk by more than two percentage points. Retail is charging the hardest, while big money is quietly pulling back.

Add to that: RSI already broke above 77, hitting overbought territory. The four-hour chart marked it as exhausting, and volatility is through the roof.

After pushing to 2529, price got pinned back. It then got smashed down to 2355 and bounced up again. That move washed the leverage layer once, and contract open interest shrank by almost 6 percentage points in a day.

Right now, the price is exactly pressing against the 24-hour high at 2467. Whether it can break through all depends on volume.

So I won’t chase. I’ll wait for a pullback to around the 2400 area to see if there’s support and follow-through. If it holds and stabilizes, then I’ll go in; if it breaks down and gets through, it means this momentum wasn’t taken up—then that’s a different story. Hold for the long term and don’t sell. For the short term, wait for a pullback before entering comfortably.

SEC issues new crypto regulations: not tightening, but clarifying the rules

The SEC has released a crypto regulatory framework, making the rules transparent; this is a long-term positive for Bitcoin.

This time, the SEC didn’t just issue another round of enforcement actions—it released an entire regulatory framework. In plain terms, it used to be “guess whether I’ll regulate,” now it’s “here’s exactly how you can play, in black and white.” For the market, the biggest change is that the long-standing problem of uncertainty may finally have a solution. In the past few years, institutions’ biggest concern wasn’t price volatility, but unclear rules—wondering when regulators might suddenly strike. The framework being put in place is equivalent to defusing part of that risk.

Market impact
- Short term: BTC is currently at $77,343.96, up only 0.08% over the past 24 hours, suggesting the news hasn’t been fully digested yet. Clear rules typically bring a first wave of sentiment repair; ETH is at $2,447.76, up 0.70% in 24 hours, and has already started to react.
- Medium term: A regulatory framework is a prerequisite for institutions to enter. After the ETF, the next step is more compliant capital flowing in—this logic chain is straightforward. The more detailed the rules are, the more money will dare to move in.

My view
I’m bullish, but not in the “sudden breakout” kind of way. This regulatory tailwind is a slow-moving factor, not a catalyst—don’t expect a single big green candle. For BTC, the key is whether $77,343.96 can be reclaimed and held; only then can the trend be considered confirmed. Below $77,343.96 is support—if it holds, the market can still remain in a strong consolidation pattern. The “follow-the-bullish” logic for ETH holds as well, and upside volatility may be greater than BTC’s. The biggest risk is that the framework details include overly strict provisions beyond expectations; then the assessment must be re-evaluated.

You all saw what happened in the market last Friday night, right. Bitcoin and Ether directly liquidated the shorts in one sweep—the technicals moved violently.

This is a classic signal of a short-term greedy top.

ETH is up nearly 30% over the week. That kind of speed has happened many times in bear-market rallies—every time right when sentiment is at its most euphoric. And then what? Then comes a long, grinding slide.

Right now, the FNG index is 66, while the weekly average is only 55—there’s a significant deviation. I’m not saying the market will collapse outright, but for people who chase in at this level, the risk-reward just isn’t worth it.

The key support is at 2313, and resistance is at 2517. How long this range-bound action will last is anyone’s guess, but the upside room is clearly smaller than the downside.

From a commercial-logic standpoint, this rally has a bottom-layer narrative support: mainstream exchanges are all pushing stablecoin payments, and Musk’s X is also going to stir the pot. This isn’t just price speculation—real application scenarios are actually being rolled out.

The problem is: of the people entering now, how many are really betting on this long-term trend? Most are simply chasing pumps and cutting at the top.

This isn’t the bottom of a bear market; it’s a mid-level rebound within a bear market. The nature hasn’t changed.

I’m not saying ETH is bad—I still believe in it long term. But if you rush in now, the risk-reward doesn’t work out.

If you already have positions, should you consider taking profit in batches? And if you’re currently in cash, wouldn’t it be better to be patient and wait for a pullback?

Put plainly: the people who truly make big money are never the ones charging in at a time like this.

U.S. House Speaker Johnson said the Iran conflict will enter a new phase, with allies becoming more deeply involved, and that the situation in the Middle East faces an escalation risk.

What’s going on
Johnson’s comments are not just being said casually. What he means is: from here on, it won’t be unilateral action by the U.S.; instead, multiple allies will step in together, and the scale and intensity of the conflict could move up a notch. In plain terms, official statements are issuing a “pre-emptive warning” for escalation—sending a signal early so the market and the public have a mental readiness. Historically, after this kind of “new phase” wording, actual actions usually follow, and the probability of the situation cooling down tends to decrease. For the market, the most direct transmission path is: conflict escalates → oil prices and safe-haven assets (gold, U.S. Treasuries) get favored → funds pull out from risk assets → high-volatility assets like BTC and ETH are the first to be reduced. BTC is currently at $77,218.13, down 0.11% in 24h; ETH is at $2,440.96. After geopolitical news is priced in, the market often goes sideways first, and then volatility increases.

Market impact
- Short term: risk-off sentiment heats up; leveraged funds exit first, and the risk of liquidation of long positions rises. BTC is likely to weaken in a range within the next 12 hours, while ETH’s volatility over the next 24 hours will expand. If there are subsequent substantive military actions, the $75,000 support level will be directly put to the test.
- Medium term: sustained geopolitical risk suppresses risk appetite; money flows toward gold and short-duration Treasuries. Incremental capital in crypto markets declines, limiting the height of any rebound. Conversely, if diplomatic efforts unexpectedly succeed, the return of safe-haven funds could become a catalyst.

My take
I’m bearish in the short term. Comments at Johnson’s level are rarely empty talk, and the probability of escalation is higher than that of cooling down. Whether BTC can hold $75,000 is the key: if it holds, it may lead to range-bound consolidation as the “bad news is already out”; if it breaks, it could quickly probe lower. ETH is relatively more resilient (up 0.55% over 24h), but in a weakening broader environment it can’t fully escape either—the area around $2,350 is the first support. 我短期看空。约翰逊这种级别的表态很少是空穴来风，局势升级概率大于降温。BTC守不守得住$75,000是关键：守住就是利空出尽的震荡，跌破可能快速下探。ETH相对抗跌（24h还涨0.55%），但大环境走弱它也躲不开，$2,350附近是第一道支撑。观望等落地比抢跑划算，地缘消息驱动的行情假动作多，追空追多都容易被扫。

Tether’s $120 million Bitcoin mining project in Uruguay falls apart: it’s not that it didn’t make money—it’s that they didn’t sign the contract

Tether’s Bitcoin mining project in Uruguay has been halted due to an electricity contract dispute. The mining site was disconnected in July 2025.

According to Reuters, Uruguay’s state-owned power utility UTE cut off electricity to Tether’s mining facility in July 2025. The reason is rather ridiculous: UTE required the signing of a revised power contract, but Tether’s representatives simply did not show up for the signing ceremony. The project’s total investment is $120 million and was meant to be an important part of Tether’s energy + mining expansion. In plain terms, it wasn’t just the electricity price that fell through—when it came time to sign, they didn’t attend. This is a direct breakdown at the process level.

Impact on the market
- Short term: A mild bearish sentiment. Tether is the issuer of USDT and also a major buyer of BTC. Its expansion plan being stymied may make the market worry that its hashrate deployment schedule will slow down. BTC is currently trading at $77,256.3 (24h -0.12%); it was already moving sideways, and this news gives the bears another talking point. ETH $2,440.64 (+0.48%) is basically unaffected.
- Medium term: Limited impact. $120 million is small relative to Tether’s reserves, and the mining rigs can be moved to other low-cost regions. But the industry signal is worth noting—contract battles between miners and power grids are getting tougher, and electricity resources are becoming scarce negotiation leverage in the mining sector.

My view
I’m bearish on BTC’s short-term trend, but the downside may be limited. BTC is consolidating around $77,256.3. Downside support is around $95.17K; a break could accelerate the move lower. $95.17K above is a clear resistance. This news alone is not enough to smash the market, but combined with the current low-volume environment, it’s more of a lukewarm bearish catalyst. I’d mainly watch and see whether Tether later relocates capacity or gives up entirely—that’s the key to judging its long-term commitment to mining.

ETH rose from more than $ 1800 a week ago to $ 2448 now, an increase of nearly $ 650.

A month ago, it was still bottoming out around $ 2300. A week ago, it was still struggling around $ 1900. And now it’s directly pulled up to $ 2448.

With this speed, whoever looks at it has to ask: “What happened? Can I still get in?”

Today, the BTC and ETH shorts got crushed—this is the message I saw. Plainly speaking, it’s a liquidity shock plus a short-term squeeze. It’s not that the fundamentals suddenly got better; the shorts were just hit.

Make sure you see the essence of this move—ETH is up 29.7% over the week. Trading volume has expanded, but think it through carefully: this happened in a backdrop of tightening liquidity. What does that imply? Institutions and smart money are unloading at high levels, while retail investors are left holding the bag. The 2021 script, repackaged and played again.

BTC’s market share is 59.1%, which shows the capital is still clustered in BTC; ETH is just following up, not leading the rally. That distinction is crucial.

Right now, ETH is at $ 2448. Resistance is $ 2517 above, and support is $ 2313 below. The FNG index is 66—market greed—but the weekly average is only 55, meaning everyone’s excitement only kicked in this week, not as a sustained trend. This kind of sentiment is often not sustainable.

I won’t say “buy or sell.” My take on this rally is:

If you already have a position, this is not a selling point, but it’s also not the time to add.

If you’re in cash with no position, hold your nerve—don’t FOMO.

Why?

After a short-term squeeze, there’s usually a consolidation and digestion period. The real good opportunities often appear after everyone cools down.

But the more critical question isn’t whether to get in right now—it’s:

**What’s the logic behind this rally? Can it actually materialize?**

Honestly, I looked into it all. I didn’t see any major breakthrough in ETH fundamentals. The ecosystem projects are still the same; TVL growth is also just so-so.
