【一周涨$ 650的ETH，还敢不敢追？】

ETH从一周前的$ 1800多到现在的$ 2448，涨幅将近$ 650。

一个月前还在$ 2300磨底，一周前还在$ 1900挣扎，现在直接拉到$ 2448。

这速度，换谁看了都得问一句："发生了什么？我还能不能上？"

今天BTC和ETH的空头被碾压，这个消息我看了。说白了就是流动性冲击+短期逼空，不是基本面突然变好了，是空头被打了。

看清楚这波的本质——一周涨29.7%，成交量放大了，但仔细想，这是在流动性收紧的背景下发生的。说明什么？机构和聪明钱在高位出货，散户在接盘。2021年的剧本，换了个包装又演了一遍。

BTC市场占比59.1%，说明资金还是在BTC扎堆，ETH只是跟涨，不是领涨。这个区别很关键。

现在ETH在$ 2448这个位置，上面$ 2517是阻力，下面$ 2313是支撑。FNG指数66，市场贪婪，但周均才55，说明大家的兴奋是这周才起来的，不是持续性的。这种情绪往往不可持续。

我不会说"要买还是卖"，这波我的判断是——

如果你手上有仓位，现在不是卖点，但也不是加仓的时候。

如果你空仓，忍着，别FOMO。

为什么？

短期逼空之后，通常会有一个震荡消化期。真正的好机会，往往在大家冷静下来之后出现。

但更关键的问题不是现在上不上，而是——

**这波涨势的逻辑是什么？能不能落地？**

说实话，我研究了一圈，没看到ETH基本面有什么重大突破。生态项目还是那些，TVL增长也一般。

所以这波大概率还是情绪+资金面驱动的，不是基本面驱动的。情绪驱动的行情，来得快，去得也快。

我现在的心态？

说真的，看空的理由一堆，但我看着这涨法，手确实有点痒。不过2021年的教训告诉我——手痒的时候往往是最危险的时候。

这次我选择看戏。

你们呢？现在什么心态？这波你们敢不敢？

translatedData.title: Bull is here? Fake breakout to wash shorts?
translatedData.subTitle: During this period, #BTC  #ETH  successive pumps have occurred, and many people have been liquidated in this rally—but is this really “bullish”? I don’t think this is a true great bull market. It’s more like a small bull that’s been built up by the buildup of short-covering from the bears. For the next stretch of time, don’t go against the market and short BTC and ETH. You can try going long in tranches between 2350 and 2090, with take-profit around 3200; the same applies to the big BTC (BTC) chart. Don’t assume this pullback will be very deep. If you’ve studied cycles, you’ll know that the “small bull” created by forcing shorts to cover through a washout is very intense. If you want to open a short position, you can enter shorts in batches between 3000 and 3300, and exit if it breaks above 3500. It will come down. Don’t blindly chase longs thinking it’s going to 5000. And don’t chase shorts just because of the pullback.

XRP surged for the week, posting its biggest weekly gain in 21 months—yet the real driver is the U.S. Treasury’s buyback

The U.S. Treasury expanded its buyback operations, warming liquidity expectations. XRP led among major coins, rising 3.49% over the past 24 hours.

The U.S. Treasury has expanded its buyback program. In simple terms, the Treasury buys back old Treasuries it holds, injecting liquidity into the market and lowering borrowing costs. Historically, this kind of move has been a genuine tailwind for risk assets: when money gets cheaper, some of it inevitably flows into the crypto market.

This time, the fastest emotion to transmit is to XRP. It is currently at $1.499, up 3.49% in 24 hours, and is breaking out of its largest single-week rally in 21 months. By comparison, BTC is only up slightly by 0.25% to $77,208, and ETH is up 1.14% to $2,441.5. The gains are concentrated in high-beta coins like XRP, suggesting capital is betting on volatility rather than seeking safety.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Looser liquidity expectations directly lift risk appetite. As a sentiment barometer, XRP has the largest upside elasticity. But BTC is unmoved around $77,208, indicating the main capital has not fully followed through yet. At this stage, more funds are rotating between coins rather than coming in as an overall incremental increase.
- Medium term: If the Treasury continues to step up buybacks, improved liquidity in U.S. Treasuries will spill over into all risk assets, including crypto. Only then will the catch-up potential for large-cap coins like BTC truly open up.

My take
I’m inclined to be bullish, but I want to look in layers. XRP’s short-term rally has already outpaced the fundamentals. Chasing higher near $1.499 generally offers mediocre odds; a pullback and confirmation would be a healthier setup. The real focus is BTC—liquidity tailwinds haven’t really been fully priced in yet. If BTC holds and builds above $77,208 with volume, the upside will be clearer than for XRP, which has already run. The risk is that if the buyback scale falls short of expectations, when sentiment turns, high-beta coins will likely drop the fastest.

- Direction: Bullish 📈 Predicting a rise
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours / XRP 4 hours

XRP单周涨出21个月最大涨幅，背后推手居然是美国财政部回购

美国财政部扩大回购操作，流动性预期升温，XRP领涨主流币，24小时涨3.49%。

美国财政部扩大了回购计划。简单讲就是财政部把手里的旧国债买回来，往市场里注入流动性，压低融资成本。历史上这种操作对风险资产是实打实的顺风：钱变便宜了，总有一部分流向加密市场。

这次情绪传导最快的是XRP，目前报$1.499，24小时涨3.49%，正在走出21个月来最大单周涨幅。相比之下BTC只微涨0.25%报$77,208，ETH涨1.14%报$2,441.5，涨幅集中在XRP这种高beta币种上，说明资金在博弹性而不是求稳。

对市场的影响
- 短期：流动性宽松预期直接抬升风险偏好，XRP作为情绪风向标弹性最大。但BTC在$77,208附近纹丝不动，说明主力资金还没全面跟进，目前更多是资金在币种间轮动，而非整体增量入场。
- 中期：如果财政部回购持续加码，美债流动性改善会传导到包括加密在内的所有风险资产，BTC这类大市值币的补涨空间才真正打开。

我的判断
我倾向看多，但要分层看。XRP短期涨幅已经领先基本面，$1.499附近追高的赔率一般，回踩确认才是更健康的走势。真正值得盯的是BTC——流动性利好它还没兑现，$77,208这个位置如果放量站稳，向上空间比已经涨完的XRP更清晰。风险点在于：回购规模如果不及预期，情绪退潮时高beta币跌得也最快。

- 币种：BTC / ETH / XRP
- 方向：利多📈 预测涨

MACD is still bullish, with DIF at 44.8—not exactly aggressive.
RSI is 51.2, neither overbought nor oversold, and the bounce hasn’t finished yet.
The Bollinger Band width has been squeezed down to 2.5%, so tight that the odds of a breakout are building up.

Above, 78,828 and 78,818 are almost stacked into a narrow resistance band.
The two resistance levels overlap, which means there’s consensus at this price—so the bears’ line of defense is right here.
Only if volume breaks through does the bull side truly “move.”
But with the early-morning liquidity like this, it can’t support a real breakout. I won’t chase.

Downside, the first line of defense is MA20 at 76,876.
If it breaks, then watch 75,872—that’s where I’m prepared to buy long.
Next level down is 75,545, the bulls’ bottom line.
If it gets pierced through, the bull thesis breaks—that won’t be catching a pin; it’ll be catching a blade.

If it fake-breaks upward to 78.8k, and there’s no volume, it’s fake. I’ll reduce there, not add.

At 75,872, should you catch this pin?

XRP sees its biggest weekly jump in 21 months—could it be due to the U.S. Treasury’s buybacks?

The Treasury expands its buyback program to boost liquidity, and XRP’s weekly gain could reach a new 21-month high.

The U.S. Treasury has expanded the scale of its bond buybacks. Put simply, the Treasury buys back old government bonds circulating in the market, injecting liquidity into it. This lowers short-term funding costs, making it more likely that money flows toward risk assets. After the news broke, market sentiment clearly improved, and XRP became the leader of this rebound. Over the past 24 hours, XRP is up 3.49% to $1.499, moving toward the largest single-week gain in 21 months. BTC is currently $77,208 (24h +0.25%), ETH is $2,441.5 (24h +1.14%), and the rebound strength is still weaker than XRP.

One-sentence translation: The Treasury is quietly “opening the taps,” and money is starting to move from safe-haven assets to risk assets.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Liquidity expectations are one of the biggest positives for the crypto market. Buybacks lower borrowing costs and reduce the funding costs for stablecoin spread trades; altcoins have the highest elasticity, and XRP’s 3.49% jump is proof.
- Medium term: If buybacks become routine, it effectively provides a liquidity floor for risk assets. But note: this is a Treasury operation, not rate cuts, so the effect is milder—don’t expect a repeat of the “flood the market” style from 2020.

My take
Bullish short term, but the strength is questionable. On a weekly basis, XRP is indeed strong, but BTC’s only +0.25% gain suggests mainstream capital is still watching from the sidelines. This looks more like an altcoin rebound rather than a full-blown turn to a bull market. While the overall stablecoin market is cooling, USDT users are surging instead. Its growth rate is nearly 3 times that of USDC.

Over the past week, Tether’s USDT added 1.6 million new holders, while USDC’s growth over the same period was less than one-third of that. The backdrop is that the stablecoin market as a whole is losing heat, with total market cap under pressure and demand weakening. But USDT’s expansion path is different from USDC’s: its home base is in emerging markets—such as Turkey, Nigeria, Argentina, and Southeast Asia—where people use USDT not to speculate on crypto, but to hedge against local-currency depreciation and for cross-border settlement. These needs aren’t affected by whether crypto market sentiment is hot or cold.

In one sentence: Wall Street’s money is pulling back, but risk-hedging demand from everyday people in the Third World is moving in.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Limited direct boost to BTC and ETH prices. More stablecoin holders ≠ an immediate rush to buy crypto. But purchasing power in emerging markets is a slow variable: the deeper USDT penetrates there, the thicker the “incoming capital pool” in the future. BTC is currently ranging around $77,208 and ETH around $2,441.5; in this kind of supply-demand standoff, new users are a small portion of the true marginal increase.
- Medium term: The stablecoin landscape becomes even more concentrated in USDT. On the regulatory front, the U.S. is pushing a compliant stablecoin bill, and USDC has strong advantages at home. However, user data shows that the real demand is happening on-chain and overseas. This contrast is worth noting for everyone watching the stablecoin track.

This is a bullish factor, but it’s a medium-term story rather than a short-term catalyst. BTC is grinding near $77,208; as long as it doesn’t break the previous low, USDT’s continued balance-sheet expansion is essentially supplying liquidity for the next leg of the market. ETH has greater upside elasticity—users entering from emerging markets typically buy major coins first. The risk is that if the total stablecoin market cap keeps shrinking, it would mean existing capital is still flowing out, and the newly added holders may not be enough to absorb it.

It’s not me trying to scare you—this is a question I’ve seriously thought through.

Back in 2018, I watched ETH fall from 1,400 to 80 RMB with my own eyes. People around me got liquidated and even jumped to their deaths. There were also “studio” models from private clubs who ended up doing menial jobs as work at the bottom. At that time, everyone said Ethereum was done and the bubble had burst. So what happened in the end?

Now we’re in a similar situation again. ETH has retraced more than 50% from its peak. In 7 days it has risen nearly 30%, with trading volume expanding abnormally—which means both longs and shorts are fiercely rotating positions. The market sentiment greed index is 66, which is a full 11 points higher than last week’s average.

After going through so many cycles in practice, here’s a fact I’ll tell you plainly: at times like this, the most dangerous thing isn’t the market itself—it’s retail investors’ judgment.

If this round of ETH can rally, on the surface it looks like a short squeeze crushing the shorts. But in my view, the real underlying reason is that the industry’s fundamentals are changing. A report by CoinDesk mentioned that banks and tech companies are moving toward stablecoins. Didn’t you understand what that signal means?

Let me be direct: ETH is not just a blockchain anymore—it’s an asset class that traditional finance is taking seriously.

The inflows after the ETF got approved may not be huge, but that’s a matter of timing and scale—it’s about attitude, not volume.

On the practical side—

For those still纠结 about “Can ETH get back to 4,000?” your direction is wrong. What you should really be thinking is: if ETH’s ecosystem truly begins to absorb the migration of RWA assets from traditional finance, what does that imply?

Big institutions are not coming in to pump coins. They’re coming to save money and streamline processes by using this infrastructure.

ETH’s current pullback, to some extent, is creating entry windows for these funds.

My take: this won’t end immediately, but it won’t be a V-shaped reversal either. More likely, it will grind higher in a range, and the real test is whether you can hold your position. If you’re trying to make quick money, I suggest you don’t enter now—this kind of market is where people are most easily chopped back and forth.

Finally, here’s a hands-on question for you: in your view, for ETH to truly take off, what it needs is not just the price going up—but what, exactly?

title: Another DeFi Hack: Term Labs Loses 8.5 Million in Governance Exploit
subTitle:
$ETH governance exploits keep proving that on-chain voting isn't a security feature - it's an attack surface. Term Labs lost 2,843 ETH and 1.68M USDC on Sunday when an attacker manipulated the protocol's governance to drain Term vaults. At current prices that's roughly 6.95M USDT in ETH plus the stablecoin haul, totaling the 8.5M figure PeckShield reported.

The mechanics are familiar: accumulate voting power, propose a malicious upgrade, execute before anyone can react. Term Labs confirmed the breach but hasn't detailed whether the attacker used flash-loaned governance tokens or exploited a quorum threshold. Either way, the vaults held user deposits directly - no timelock, no multisig guardian, just a single proposal execution.

This marks the third notable governance drain this quarter. Protocols treating governance as a feature rather than a liability keep learning the same lesson. If your treasury or user funds can be moved by a single on-chain vote without a 48-hour timelock and multisig veto, you're not decentralized - you're a honeypot.

The OCC has granted a license to a stablecoin trust company with a Trump family background. The family has upgraded from issuing meme coins to holding a licensed crypto bank.

Clearly bullish; there’s only one reason: political resources are concentrating toward the stablecoin track. This is a window we haven’t seen in the past four years. For spot, in the last three hours, there have been twelve candles and none have gone negative. In the fifteen-minute chart, the big orders are still in net inflow—money really did come in, and it can’t be denied.

The problem is on the futures side. In one day, open interest shrank by almost 6%. Aggressive sell orders are pressing down on buys, and longs are pulling out. The funding rate is flat. On the order book, buy orders are still layered fairly thickly, so it’s not easy to smash it down. But this spot is only one step away from today’s high. It keeps touching and then shrinking back—day by day it gets more timid. The more it rises to this extent, the less it’s worth pushing.

ETH is hovering around 2445 now—up nearly 30% over the week. It’s been a run from 1868 all the way to 2549. The move has definitely been aggressive. But first, my conclusion: the direction isn’t broken—don’t rush to chase at this level.

The key is that futures and spot are basically fighting each other. On the futures side, it’s clearly deleveraging: open interest dropped nearly 6% in a day, the funding rate got slammed back to 0.01%, and the on-chain lending ratio plunged by almost 80% within 12 hours. In plain terms: the leverage that chased earlier highs has been mostly wiped out. This isn’t a panic collapse—it’s “clearing hazards” while the uptrend continues.

But the spot side is still buying. Over a 3-hour window, all 12 candlesticks saw net inflows. The buy-wall in the top 20 price levels is more than five times thicker than the sell-wall, and the aggressive bid pressure is pressing down on the ask. The money hasn’t fled—it’s just switched hands and is being used to support.

The risk is also right in front of us: RSI has pushed up to 77 and continues higher, volatility is off the charts, futures’ active selling is amplifying, and the 1-hour chart is still probing downward. After a 30% jump, a spike-and-retrace or grinding sideways for a while is the normal script.

My stance: the trend hasn’t broken, and the 7-day outlook won’t end just because of a single bearish candle—but the risk/reward for going long here isn’t great. A more comfortable approach is to wait for a pullback, then confirm that spot is still holding support and that the dip isn’t deep before going in. Don’t rush to board, and don’t panic about getting off.

ETH: In a choppy/sideways regime, keep a light position or stay on the sidelines until the direction becomes clear. Don’t let boredom force you to act.

BTC is still a BULL_TREND. Note that I said “still”—it’s down 0.4% over 24 hours, and many people are starting to doubt. But the trend isn’t broken by one early-session dip; it’s broken by a series of structural failures. Right now, the structure hasn’t failed.

ETH is CHOP_MID. The kind that’s messy. The higher highs and lower lows don’t point anywhere, OI is drifting around. This kind of market most easily makes people get hit from both sides—going long gets shaken out, going short gets run over. Best choice: don’t trade.

━━━ Psychological Traps ━━━
Just after the weekend, many people enter with weekend FOMO. They see BTC dip slightly and think, “Opportunity is here.” In fact, this is the most dangerous time—because your judgment is contaminated by emotion, not logic.

Fear and greed don’t kill people. Confusing the two kills people.

━━━ Strategic Direction ━━━
BTC: the trend isn’t broken—participate on pullbacks, don’t chase.
ETH: CHOP regime—wait for a confirmed breakout; otherwise, observe.

I’ve seen too many people grind away profits in CHOP, and then miss the real trend move.

讲真，涨幅榜前三个我上周都在关注，MORPHO的7d+38.6%已经是明牌了，但SPK这波3.5倍放量拉升是真没想到。让我想起上个月错过AAVE那波，当时也是量能突然放大，我没敢追，结果眼睁睁看着它从170一路干到200多（说多了都是泪）。

先聊SPK。0.0217的价格，现在卡在区间70%的位置，24h高点0.02415，支撑在0.02135。放量3.5倍，这个量能配合22.98%的涨幅，市场共识是"强者恒强"。但逆向思维一下，量能这么大，说明分歧也大，有人疯狂买就有人在疯狂卖。短线偏多思路的话，0.02135不破可以看，止损放0.0208下方，第一目标0.02415，盈亏比大概1:2.5。但注意，这币如果回踩0.02135的时候缩量，那就是健康洗盘；要是放量砸穿，直接认错离场，别犹豫。资金费率目前正常，没有过热迹象，说明这波拉升不是杠杆堆出来的，相对健康。

MORPHO，2.7463，这个位置有点尴尬。区间78%处，离阻力2.936就差一口气，但7d已经涨了38.6%，短线追高的性价比其实一般。中线视角看，DeFi借贷赛道Morpho确实是优质标的，TVL增长逻辑还在。但如果要进场，我倾向于等回踩2.676附近再看，止损2.55，目标先看2.936，盈亏比接近1:2。交易失效条件就是跌破2.55且日线收不回来，那说明这波行情暂时结束了。顺便说一句，MORPHO资金费率0.005%，很健康，没有过热迹象。

LIT这个币，涨幅榜第三但位置最尴尬。当前价3.6502，区间96%处，基本贴着24h高点3.701在走。这种位置追进去，跟买彩票差不多，冲高回落留根长上影你就知道什么叫难受了。我宁可错过也不想在96%的位置接盘。除非它放量突破3.701并且站稳，那才考虑追，否则看戏就好。

大盘这边，BTC 77,016，ETH 2,430，7d分别+23.4%和+31.3%，这个背景下山寨币集体开花很正常。恐惧贪婪指数50，Neutral，这个位置很有意思——既不是FOMO也不是恐慌，说明市场还有分歧，反而是好事。我最怕的是指数冲到75以上的时候，那才是真正该小心的时候。

今天跌幅榜上GRVT -11.14%，资金费率-0.0755%，空头已经过热了。这种负费率+价格下跌的组合，往往是短期反弹的前兆，但我不建议去抄底，逆势接刀子的活我干过太多次了，疼。

我的结论：整体情绪偏暖但没到疯狂，精选标的做，别贪。SPK回踩不破可以轻仓尝试，MORPHO等回调，LIT看戏。大家现在都在追涨幅榜，我反而想看看那些被冷落的板块有没有机会，比如RWA相关的，最近好像有点动静。

你们怎么看这波SPK的放量拉升？是真突破还是诱多？评论区聊聊。

A US banking industry group proposes including the stablecoin secondary market in identity verification

The American Bankers Policy Institute has recently submitted comments to the US Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, suggesting that customer identity verification requirements for stablecoin customers be extended from the issuance stage to the secondary market. The organization represents major banks including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and Citibank, and argues that the stablecoin compliance boundary should be pushed back into public discussion.

Against this backdrop, the proposed debate reflects continued expansion in the use of payment-type stablecoins in transaction settlement and cross-border payments, with anti-money laundering (AML) and customer due diligence coverage emerging as a shared focus for both regulators and traditional financial institutions. In related proposed discussions, regulators have noted that transactions in stablecoin blockchain secondary markets often feature anonymous or pseudo-anonymous characteristics, with no centralized identity information collection nodes. They have also pointed out that issuers have relatively limited capability to obtain secondary-market customer data. It is precisely amid this combination of regulatory gaps and operational difficulties that the banking industry group has put forward clear policy recommendations.

On the core facts, the American Bankers Policy Institute believes that exchanges and other platforms that establish direct account relationships with retail investors carry out most of the buying and selling activity in the stablecoin payment ecosystem, and that much of the illegal financial activity related to stablecoins occurs in the secondary market. Therefore, the organization recommends extending customer identity verification program requirements to these secondary-market entities, so they can collect user identity information under the Bank Secrecy Act. Reports further indicate that if the proposal is incorporated into formal rules, decentralized trading platforms could also fall under the regulatory scope. What needs to be clearly distinguished is that the above content represents feedback from an industry association to regulators; it does not equate to final regulations that have already taken effect. Whether regulators adopt it, and how they implement it in which wording, remains uncertain.

From a logical breakdown, the substance of this proposal is a reallocation of compliance responsibility. The traditional banking system has relatively mature infrastructure for customer identity verification and suspicious transaction monitoring, whereas after stablecoin issuance, circulation relies heavily on trading platforms, wallets, and on-chain protocols. On the one hand, the banking industry group acknowledges that the secondary market is a relatively high-risk area; on the other hand, it argues that the platforms that establish account relationships with retail customers should bear the identity collection obligation. This aligns with the regulatory logic of: “who is closer to the transaction, who has better conditions for collecting information, and therefore who should assume the corresponding duties.” However, in decentralized settings, how to define “account relationship” and how to implement real-name identity information collection still face dual technical and legal barriers. Regulators’ prior judgment that identity data collection in secondary markets is “challenging in practice” also indicates that feasibility issues have been included in the discussion and will not simply be ignored.

Possible pathways of impact on the crypto market can be observed from several angles. First, if future rules clearly require centralized trading platforms to conduct stricter identity verification for stablecoin-related accounts, compliance costs and user account-opening barriers may increase, and some demand focused on process convenience or cross-border usage may reassess trading channels. Second, if decentralized trading is substantially brought under the same customer identity verification framework, the protocol access layer, front-end entry points, or liquidity aggregation stages may be forced to add compliance components, thereby changing the way permissionless interactions operate today. Third, for licensed stablecoin issuers, if secondary-market responsibility is borne more by exchanges and account platforms, the compliance boundaries on the primary issuance side may be relatively clearer; however, as overall market compliance strength increases, it could also reinforce a split between well-regulated circulation channels and weaker-regulation channels. All of the above are scenario analyses based on currently available public information, not definitive judgments about regulatory outcomes or market trends.

In an editor’s view, the core of the current debate is not simply whether to strengthen AML, but how AML obligations should be divided across issuance, trading, custody, and protocol layers—and whether the division criteria match technical executability. By shining a light on the secondary market, the banking industry group’s proposal can help drive public discussion among regulators, issuers, and trading platforms about the boundaries of responsibility. But if rule design overlooks the real constraints of on-chain pseudo-anonymous transactions, non-custodial wallets, and cross-border platforms, a mismatch could arise between compliance requirements and execution capability. Going forward, attention should be paid to whether regulators absorb such input, how the final text defines secondary-market entities, and what interpretation would apply to decentralized platforms. Until rules are finalized, market participants would generally be better advised to focus on understanding policy signals and improving their own compliance preparations, rather than over-interpreting short-term market moves.

#BPI吁FinCEN扩大稳定币身份识别至二级市场 #BTC #ETH #BNB

content:
美国银行业团体提议将稳定币二级市场纳入身份识别

美国银行政策研究所近日向美国财政部金融犯罪执法网络提交意见，建议将稳定币客户身份识别要求从发行环节延伸到二级市场。该组织代表摩根大通、美国银行、富国银行、花旗等大型银行，其主张把稳定币合规边界再次推入公开讨论。

从事件背景看，支付型稳定币在交易结算与跨境支付中的使用持续扩大，反洗钱与客户尽职调查覆盖范围成为监管与传统金融机构共同关注的焦点。相关拟议讨论中，监管层已指出：稳定币在区块链二级市场的交易往往呈现匿名或伪匿名特征，缺少集中化的身份信息采集节点，发行方获取二级市场客户数据的能力也相对有限。正是在制度空白与操作难点并存的背景下，银行业团体给出了明确政策建议。

核心事实方面，美国银行政策研究所认为，交易所及其他与零售投资者建立直接账户关系的平台，承担了稳定币支付生态中的大部分买卖活动，且多数与稳定币相关的非法金融活动发生在二级市场。因此，该组织建议将客户身份识别计划要求扩展至这些二级市场主体，使其依据《银行保密法》收集用户身份信息。有报道进一步指出，若相关提议被纳入正式规则，去中心化交易平台也可能被纳入管理范围。需要明确区分的是，上述内容属于行业协会对监管机构的意见反馈，并不等于已经生效的最终法规，监管机构是否采纳、以何种口径落地仍不确定。

从逻辑拆解看，这一主张的实质是重新分配合规责任。传统银行体系拥有较为成熟的客户身份识别与可疑交易监测基础设施，而稳定币发行后的流通高度依赖交易平台、钱包与链上协议。银行业团体一方面承认二级市场是风险相对集中的区域，另一方面主张由与零售客户建立账户关系的平台承担身份采集义务，这与“谁更接近交易、谁更具备信息采集条件，谁就应承担相应义务”的监管思路相吻合。但在去中心化场景下，如何界定账户关系、如何落实实名信息采集，仍存在技术与法律双重障碍。监管层此前关于二级市场身份采集“实际操作具有挑战性”的判断，也说明可行性问题已被纳入讨论，并不会被简单忽视。

对加密市场的影响路径，可从几个层面观察。第一，若未来规则明确要求中心化交易平台对稳定币相关账户执行更严格的身份识别，合规成本与用户开户门槛可能上升，部分注重流程便利或跨境使用的需求或将重新评估交易渠道。第二，若去中心化交易被实质性纳入同一套客户身份识别框架，协议接入层、前端入口或流动性聚合环节可能被迫增加合规组件，从而改变现有无许可交互的运行方式。第三，对持牌稳定币发行方而言，若二级市场责任更多由交易与账户平台承担，一级发行端的合规边界或相对清晰；但市场整体合规强度上升，也可能强化合规流通渠道与弱监管渠道之间的分层。以上均为基于现有公开信息的路径推演，并非对监管结果或市场走势的断定。

编辑判断认为，当前争论的核心并不只是要不要强化反洗钱，而是反洗钱义务在发行、交易、托管与协议层之间如何切分，以及切分标准是否与技术可执行性匹配。银行业团体的建议把二级市场推到聚光灯下，有助于促使监管、发行方与交易平台公开讨论责任边界；但若规则设计忽视链上伪匿名交易、非托管钱包与跨境平台的现实约束，可能出现合规要求与执行能力错配。后续仍需关注监管机构是否吸收此类意见、最终文本如何定义二级市场主体，以及去中心化平台的适用口径。在规则尚未落地前，市场参与者更宜把重点放在理解政策信号与完善自身合规准备，而不是对短期波动作过度解读。

这是典型的对冲套利打法：开空单赌跌，同时持有现货对冲部分风险，赚的是价格波动和资金费率的钱。说白了人家不一定是纯看空，但这种体量的仓位一旦有动作，市场必然跟着晃。

一句话翻译：大资金在为下跌做准备，顺便把ETH现货提到自己钱包里防止被清算连坐。

对市场的影响
- 短期：7.83亿美元空单摆在链上，所有人都能看到。这种透明度反而放大恐慌，散户会先跑为敬，ETH在$2,451.27这个位置压力陡增。BTC目前在$77,401.64横着，但如果ETH被砸下去，很难独善其身。
- 中期：巨鲸利用Hyperliquid这种链上平台做大规模对冲，说明衍生品流动性在往链上迁移。但也暴露了一个问题：单一平台承接这么大仓位，一旦剧烈波动，连环清算的破坏力不小。

我的判断
明确偏空。空单规模远大于提取的现货对冲规模（7.83亿 vs 1.73亿），净敞口是看跌的。ETH上方$2,500是短期阻力，跌破$2,451.27大概率加速；BTC守住$94.73K还算是健康回调，破了就要看$94.73K。

这种巨鲸仓位本身就是信号，不一定要跟随，但不能装看不见。

$BTC isn’t rising quickly, yet $ETH’s contract open interest expands first: with the same ETF tailwind, why does the market price the risk first into ETH?

The facts: In Binance USDT-margined perpetuals, $BTC in the past 24 hours is $77,482, up 0.27%, with about $10.39 billion in trading volume; $ETH is $2,454, up 1.11%, with about $10.98 billion in trading volume. Funding reality: Farside reported that on August 21, US spot ETF net inflows were $307.5 million for BTC and $184.0 million for ETH, totaling about $491.5 million. BTC received more allocation capital, but these figures are the settlement from the previous trading day in US equities—they don’t automatically determine which contract will gain strength first over the weekend.

The real-time difference shows up in positioning. Over the last two hours, BTC’s open-interest notional value is about +0.59%, rising from $8.16 billion to $8.20 billion; ETH is about +1.07%, from $5.83 billion to $5.89 billion. ETH’s price increase is larger, and its open-interest growth is faster. It could mean longs are actively adding, or it could mean both longs and shorts are pushing volatility higher; open interest by itself doesn’t tell you the answer.

So the divergence between the tailwind and price action is not contradictory. ETF inflows set the “background color” for positioning, while short-term trading is driven by liquidity, volatility expectations, and which side is more easily pushed by leverage. The market is confirming: can ETH’s added risk turn into sustained spot absorption, or is it only amplifying a burst of volatility when weekend liquidity is thinner?

For the bulls to be right, ETH needs to stay relatively strong, trading volume must keep expanding, open interest should increase while funding rates remain restrained—while BTC also doesn’t weaken. For the bears to be right, ETH needs to pull back first, open interest still climbs, funding rates rise but BTC doesn’t keep up; that would suggest contract “heat” is higher than spot confirmation. The most common mistake ordinary traders make is translating an increase in ETH positions directly into “the long side wins for sure.”

My view: I’m more inclined to watch whether ETH’s relative strength versus BTC can carry over into the next round of expanded trading, rather than chasing hour-by-hour position increases. If price and volume can’t sync, increased positions can actually heighten the impact during liquidation. Risk warning: leverage and insufficient liquidity can amplify slippage—keep risk light and set a stop-loss in advance.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  I watched the @Dusk_Foundation  whitepaper for two nights, and the more I think about it, the more afraid I get. Everyone is now watching to see whether so-called “privacy compliance” can actually be implemented, but the direction has already gone completely off course. The real soul-searching question we should figure out right now is: who, behind the scenes, is holding the power to decide the fate of your wallet and whether you live or die?

In mid-August, the team said that just fiddling with asset splitting won’t fool or attract big capital—we must tightly bind together the entire process of opening accounts, buying and selling, and settlement. That pitch sounds quite reasonable from a business standpoint, right? But the more you dig into their architecture, the more your scalp crawls.

Even the base layer of the mainnet directly includes a super backdoor for “forced asset transfers” and “changing the account ledger from the backend.” And look at that Citadel mechanism: if you want to interact on-chain, you have to see whether the licensed institutions in the real world give you the green light. Service providers can even cut off your network access instantly with a single command. So what kind of decentralization is this? It’s simply copying the traditional finance black-box system onto the chain. I understand that achieving compliance requires administrators, but where exactly are the boundaries of their power? Who decides when it’s allowed to confiscate users’ assets? If offline institutions collude to do harm, who compensates the victims? How are the issuer and the operator supposed to check and balance each other? None of that is spelled out.

People with good memory probably haven’t forgotten the tragedy that happened back in January this year: all it took was a single-signed private key not being properly protected, and the hacker was like strolling through a street market—taking away nearly 10.91 million DUSK with ease. Afterward, the official even did a self-critique: putting your entire fortune and life on a single node is basically asking for disaster. They can’t even keep the door to their own vault under control, and now they want to use this same setup to take full control of the retail investors’ underwear?

So, don’t sell me grand blueprints about big institutions coming in—I’m not buying it. My only requirement at the moment is: let the official publish a clear, unambiguous diagram of how permissions are allocated. ZK algorithms can indeed obscure data, and a compliance framework can handle regulators, but for a fundamental principle like “why someone else is allowed to directly transfer my coins,” they absolutely must not be allowed to hand-wave it away. #eth $ETH

这哪是去中心化？简直是把传统金融那套黑箱“守门员”玩法原封不动搬到了链上。搞合规确实需要引入管理员，但关键在于，这把尚方宝剑到底谁来挥？触犯什么具体条款才会被强制没收资产？线下节点如果联手作恶，谁来买单？发牌方和运营方之间又靠什么来互相制衡？这些全是一笔糊涂账。

别忘了今年1月份那场闹剧：仅仅因为单点签名的私钥被攻破，黑客轻轻松松就顺走了大约 1091 万枚 DUSK。事后团队自己也反省，把资金安全挂在一根线上就是送人头。连最基本的金库大门都守不住，现在居然想用这套脆弱的班底来全盘接管用户的“后门”？

所以，不管现在他们怎么画“华尔街机构进场”的大饼，我是一口都吃不下了。我只求一份公开透明的权限关系图。ZK技术保密确实好用，法律条文也能应付审查，但在“凭啥你能一键划走我的币”这个死穴上，决不允许有任何和稀泥的空间。#eth $ETH

Central banks around the world begin collectively warning about dollar stablecoins; this time the target is monetary policy sovereignty

Officials from multiple central banks worry that dollar stablecoins could sideline domestic monetary policy, creating a short-term sentiment headwind for the crypto market.

According to Crypto Briefing, a group of central bank officials has publicly voiced concerns: the expansion of dollar stablecoins may allow local residents to bypass their national currency and directly hold dollar-denominated digital assets—effectively completing “dollarization” on-chain. This is especially deadly for countries with high inflation. Once residents get used to storing value and making payments with stablecoins, the central bank’s interest-rate tools and money-supply controls become essentially ineffective. In plain terms, this is a direct collision between sovereign currencies and on-chain dollars—not a technical debate, but a fight over monetary discourse power.

Market impact

- Medium term: The real variable will be whether central banks accelerate their own CBDC rollouts to counter stablecoins, with the regulatory framework becoming clearer. Long-term pressure is likely for issuers such as Circle and Tether, but for BTC it could be a narrative positive—increasing central-bank anxiety signals that decentralized assets have hit a real pain point.

My view
Near term: neutral to slightly bearish. Within the next 12 hours, I don’t think this can send BTC into a deep downside plunge. Holding the $76,000 area is a show of strength and consolidation. Medium term: bullish. Central banks’ anxiety is precisely the backing for crypto’s value proposition. As the primary network for stablecoin settlement, ETH has key support around the $2,400 level—only a breakdown would indicate weakness.

Why do dollar stablecoins worry central banks about monetary sovereignty?

Multiple central banks have warned that dollar stablecoins are eroding their domestic monetary policy, which is sentimentally bullish for BTC/ETH in the short term.

According to Crypto Briefing, central bank officials have spoken out collectively: the expansion of dollar stablecoins is threatening their monetary sovereignty. Put simply, the more widely stablecoins pegged to the US dollar—such as USDT and USDC—circulate globally (especially in emerging markets), the more local people effectively end up holding the US dollar. That in turn sidelines domestic currency deposits and interest-rate control. When central banks raise rates to fight inflation, people turn around and buy stablecoins—the policy directly fails.

Impact on the market
- Short term: In essence, this is yet another official endorsement of the stablecoin’s status—even central banks admit it has grown so large that it threatens sovereignty. Sentiment is bullish for BTC $77,687.99 and ETH $2,461.22, and the market is red today too (XRP 24h +3.51%). However, the impact level is limited and won’t directly trigger a major market move.
- Medium term: Two paths—either countries accelerate the development of their own CBDCs to counter it, or they tighten regulation on dollar stablecoins. In emerging markets (countries with high inflation such as Turkey, Nigeria, and Argentina), demand for stablecoins would be even more rigid. A portion of this capital will ultimately flow into BTC.

My take
My view: neutral to bullish. Central banks say it threatens sovereignty, but none can come up with an effective blocking measure—the penetration of dollar stablecoins will only continue. As long as BTC holds the $75K level, the trend is intact. The upside is whether it can hold above $80K. ETH has support around $2,400. The real risk isn’t this news, but rather a sudden hard ban policy from some country—that would trigger short-term risk-off selling pressure.

One-sentence translation: Central banks oppose it, which actually proves the stablecoin “pipeline” can’t be shut off—and at the end of the pipeline is often BTC.

Crypto Briefing报道，各国央行官员集体发声：美元稳定币的扩张正在威胁他们的货币主权。说白了，就是USDT、USDC这类锚定美元的稳定币在全球（尤其新兴市场）流通越广，当地人等于变相持有了美元，本币的存款、利率调控都会被架空。央行加息抗通胀，老百姓转头买稳定币，政策直接失灵。

对市场的影响
- 短期：这消息本质是对稳定币地位的又一次官方背书——连央行都承认它已经大到威胁主权了。对BTC $77,687.99、ETH $2,461.22偏情绪利好，市场今天也是红的（XRP 24h +3.51%）。但影响级别有限，不会直接砸出大行情。
- 中期：两条路——要么各国加速推自己的CBDC对抗，要么收紧对美元稳定币的监管。新兴市场（土耳其、尼日利亚、阿根廷这类高通胀国家）的稳定币需求反而会更刚性，这部分资金最终不少会流向BTC。

我的判断
我的观点：中性偏多。央行嘴上喊威胁，但没一个能拿出有效的封堵方案，美元稳定币的渗透只会继续。BTC守住$75K一线则趋势未坏，上方看能否站稳$80K；ETH在$2,400附近有承接。真正的风险不是这条新闻，而是某国突然出台硬性封杀政策，那会引发短期避险抛压。

一句话翻译：央行反对，恰恰证明稳定币这条管道已经拆不掉了，而管道的尽头往往是BTC。

【History won’t repeat in a simple way, but the script always gets re-staged】

After the Spring Festival in 2019, ETH went from $120 to $280 in two months. I was there the whole time. What was the script back then? The year before had dropped by nearly 90%, and everyone thought crypto was finished—then suddenly liquidity improved, regulators started blowing warm breezes, and shorts were forced to close. A sharp rally buried all the bears.

Now the price action carries that same familiar taste.

Up 31% in a week, with trading volume expanding to more than 5% of market cap—short squeeze stacked with a loosening of regulation. This isn’t retail chasing; it’s institutions taking action.

I think over the next 7 days, ETH is likely bullish, with a grind upward amid consolidation.

Three reasons.

First, volume speaks. If the price is up 31% and can keep increasing volume, it means this isn’t a pump-and-dump to unload—it’s truly new money being absorbed. This kind of momentum won’t end in just one or two days.

Second, the 50% retracement zone is a psychological anchor for long-term capital. The 2019 rebound also started from that range. Valuations are cheap now, so institutions think it’s worth looking at.

Third, stablecoin penetration is rising—this is a signal of incremental capital entering. Musk’s X is set to pay creators with stablecoins, and banks are pushing too. This trend suggests crypto applications are expanding.

When would I admit I’m wrong? Simple: if ETH quickly breaks below the support at 2313, then drifts lower on shrinking volume—meaning this move is only a rebound, not a reversal. Then I’ll adjust my judgment.

Honestly, whether this market can truly take root depends on whether stablecoins can move from being a trading tool to a daily payment method. If they can, then today’s price is basically a floor. If they can’t, then it’s just another gimmick for rotating capital.

What do you think about this move? Is it a real industry inflection point—or just another capital game?

【历史不会简单重复，但剧本总在重演】

2019年春节后，ETH从120刀用两个月拉到280刀，那波我全程在场。当时的剧本是什么？前一年跌了快90%，所有人都觉得crypto完了，然后突然流动性改善，监管吹暖风，空头被迫平仓，一波急拉把看空的全部埋了。

现在的走势，那个味道太熟悉了。

一周涨31%，成交量放大到市值5%以上，short squeeze叠加监管松动——这不是散户在追，是机构在动手。

我判断未来7天，ETH偏看涨，震荡向上。

理由三个。

第一，成交量说话。价格涨了31%还能继续放量，说明不是拉高出货，是真的有资金在接。这种力度不会一两天就结束。

第二，50%回撤区是长线资金的心理锚点。2019年的反弹也是从这个区间启动的。估值便宜了，机构就觉得可以看了。

第三，stablecoin渗透率在上升，这是增量资金进场的信号。Musk的X要付创作者stablecoin，银行也在推——这个趋势意味着crypto的应用场景在扩大。

什么情况我会认错？很简单，如果ETH快速跌破2313这个支撑，缩量阴跌，说明这波只是反弹不是反转，我就会修正判断。

说真的，这波行情能不能真落地，关键看stablecoin能不能从交易工具变成日常支付手段。如果能，那现在的价格就是地板价；如果不能，那又是一次资金轮转的噱头。

你怎么看这波？是真的行业拐点，还是又一个资金游戏？

التداول في سوق الرقميات ليس مجرد ضربة حظ أو لحاق بـ "تريند" صاعد؛ بل هو لعبة إدارة مخاطر بالدرجة الأولى. الفرق الوحيد بين المتداول الناجح والمتداول الذي يخسر حسابه في أيام معدودة هو مدى التزامه بقواعد حماية رأس المال.
سواء كنت تتداول في السوق الفوري (Spot) أو العقود الآجلة (Futures)، إليك الدليل العملي لبناء استراتيجية إدارة مخاطر محكمة وبخطوات بسيطة.
1. قاعدة الـ 1% إلى 2% (لا تخاطر بكل شيء)
أهم قاعدة في التداول: لا تضع في الصفقة الواحدة أكثر من 1% إلى 2% من إجمالي رأس مالك.
مثال: إذا كان حسابك يحتوي على 1,000 دولار، فإن أقصى خسارة تقبلها في الصفقة الواحدة يجب ألا تتجاوز 10 إلى 20 دولارًا.
الهدف: هذه القاعدة تضمن لك البقاء في السوق حتى لو تعرضت لسلسلة خسائر متتالية.
2. أمر وقف الخسارة (Stop-Loss) هو حبل النجاة
التداول بدون أمر وقف خسارة يشبه قيادة سيارة مسرعة بدون فرامل.
في التداول الفوري (Spot): يحميك من الهبوط الحاد للعملة ويوفر لك السيولة لإعادة الشراء من أسعار أقل.
في العقود الآجلة (Futures): هو أداة إجبارية لمنع التصفية (Liquidation) وتصفير الحساب.
نصيحة: حدد نقطة الخروج بناءً على التحليل الفني (مثل الدعم والمقاومة) قبل أن تفتح الصفقة، ولا تحرك أمر وقف الخسارة للأسفل أبدًا أثناء هبوط السعر!
3. الاختلاف الجوهري بين Spot و Futures وكيف تدير مخاطرهما
التداول الفوري (Spot):
طبيعة المخاطرة: تنحصر في انخفاض قيمة العملة وليس فقدان عددها.
الاستراتيجية: يعتمد على الرافعة المالية العادية (1x)، ويمكنك فيه استخدام استراتيجية التجميع الزمني (DCA) والشراء من مناطق الدعم القوية دون قلق من تصفية الحساب.
العقود الآجلة (Futures):
طبيعة المخاطرة: عالية جدًا لإمكانية تصفية الحساب كاملاً وخسارة رأس المال في لحظات.
الاستراتيجية: تعتمد على وجود رافعة مالية تضاعف الأرباح والمخاطر، لذا تتطلب التزامًا صارمًا بـ Stop-Loss وحساب حجم الصفقة (Position Size) بدقة متناهية مع استخدام رافعة منخفضة (2x - 5x).
4. نسبة المخاطرة إلى المكافأة (Risk-to-Reward Ratio)
قبل أن تضغط على زر الشراء، احسب دائمًا: ما الذي سأكسبه مقابل ما قد أخسره؟
احرص دائمًا على أن تكون النسبة 1:2 على الأقل.
معنى ذلك: إذا كانت مخاطرتك في الصفقة 10 دولارات، فيجب أن يكون هدف الربح المحتمل 20 دولارًا على الأقل. بهذه الطريقة، حتى لو كانت نسبة نجاح صفقاتك 50% فقط، ستخرج بربح إجمالي على المدى الطويل.
5. فخ الرافعة المالية العالية في Futures
الرافعة المالية أداة ممتازة للتحكم في رأس المال، لكن استخدام رافعة مثل 20x أو 50x يحول التداول إلى مقامرة.
الرافعة العالية تقرب مستوى التصفية من سعر الدخول، مما يجعل حركة بسيطة ضد اتجاهك تنهي حسابك.
القاعدة الذهبية: اعتمد على رافعات منخفضة (من 2x إلى 5x كحد أقصى) وركز على إدارة حجم الصفقة بدلاً من زيادة الرافعة.
6. انضباط النفس والسيطرة على المشاعر
إدارة المخاطر ليست أرقامًا فقط، بل هي ضبط للنفس:
تجنب التداول الانتقامي (Revenge Trading): لا تحاول استرداد الخسارة فورًا بصفقة عشوائية.
احذر من الـ FOMO: لا تدخل صفقة ارتفعت بالفعل لمجرد الخوف من فوات الفرصة.
ضع خطة واضحة: اعرف سعر الدخول، وقف الخسارة، وجني الأرباح قبل البدء.
تذكر دائمًا: الحفاظ على رأس المال أولوية، وصنع الأرباح يأتي ثانياً. 🎯

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  A recent recap of the @Dusk_Foundation  model: I realized the thing I care about most is no longer whether the technology can work, but a very practical question—if its ecosystem really explodes in the future, how much “broth” can the $DUSK  addresses holding tokens actually drink?

If you dig into the token distribution, the total supply is fixed at 1 billion. The initial launch is 500 million tokens, and the remainder will be released gradually over the next 36 years. In the first four years, the output is maintained at roughly 19.8574 DUSK per block. The project’s intention is pretty clear: in the early stages, it must front enough inflation to feed the nodes, digging a deep moat for the underlying network’s security.

The tricky part is this. At the moment, the most tangible uses of DUSK boil down to two things: serving as Gas and participating in staking. And the block reward, in essence, is “system-issued inflation plus user transaction fees.” Of this money, miners take the lion’s share, the developer fund cleanly and consistently grabs 10%, and the rest is distributed among various committees. That means even if fees are higher, it’s still basically left hand to right hand inside the ecosystem—there’s no simple, brutal burn/destroy mechanism. The token’s inflation rate is out in the open, but whether demand for the token can keep up is something we can only take it one step at a time.

Dusk right now has been focusing on real-world assets (RWA) and the private placement market, and I’m very optimistic about this path. But everyone needs to stay clear-headed: “assets circulating on-chain” and “mass token consumption” are two completely different concepts. When traditional financial institutions come to do settlement, how many tokens do they actually need to buy to hold as reserves? Can everyday trading form a steady stream of buy orders in the secondary market? Those figures are the real headline for the future.

We’re past the stage where you can just pump the price with a roadmap—you have to lock down the real economic cycle: how much Gas is consumed per month? Has the real share of transaction fees in node revenues increased? If these key metrics stay lifeless, then no matter how much the market talks up the halving expectations, it’s, in plain terms, just pushing the bitter effects of inflation further into the future.

I’m writing this not to bash Dusk at all. In fact, because it’s tackling the hard nut of “compliant finance,” it can’t be vague about how the token captures value. The entry of major traditional institutions is indeed a team success—but only when this cooperation converts into genuine, measurable DUSK demand can token holders truly see profits. #eth $ETH

content:
#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  最近复盘 @Dusk_Foundation 的模型，我发现自己最关心的早就不再是技术能不能行，而是个很现实的问题：假如未来它的生态真的爆发了，手里拿着 $DUSK 的人到底能跟着喝到多少汤？

扒开它的筹码分布看，总量定死在 10 亿。首发 5 亿枚，剩下的准备用 36 年的时间慢慢释放。眼下前四年的产出维持在 19.8574 DUSK/块左右。项目方的意图很清晰，前期必须掏出足够的通胀来喂饱节点，先把底层网络的安全护城河给挖深。

但棘手的问题就在这儿。目前DUSK最实在的作用无非两点：充当 Gas 和参与质押。而每个区块的奖励，本质是“系统增发加上用户交易费”。在这笔钱里，矿工吃大头，开发基金雷打不动抽走 10%，剩下再给各个委员会分润。这意味着手续费再多，也仅仅是在生态内部左手倒右手，并没有简单粗暴的销毁机制。代币的通胀速度是明牌，但用币的需求能不能跟上，只能走一步看一步。

Dusk 现阶段一直在主攻现实世界资产（RWA）和私募市场，这条路我很看好。但大家得保持清醒：“资产在链上流转”和“代币被海量消耗”完全是两个概念。传统金融机构来做结算，到底需要买多少代币做储备？日常交易能不能在二级市场形成源源不断的买单？这些数据才是未来的重头戏。

现在已经不是光靠路线图就能拉盘的阶段了，得盯死真实的经济循环：单月究竟消耗了多少 Gas？真实手续费在节点收入中的占比有没有变高？如果这些关键数据死气沉沉，那未来再怎么炒作减半预期，说白了也只是把通胀的苦果往后延罢了。

我写这些绝非唱空 Dusk，正因为它做的是“合规金融”这块硬骨头，代币怎么捕获价值才更不能含糊其辞。传统大机构入局确实是团队的成功，但只有当这种合作转化为真实的DUSK需求，咱们持币者才能真正跟着吃肉。#eth $ETH

translatedData.content: 07:29｜ETH current price 2,455.76, +0.29% over the last 15 minutes. Bulls are watching 2,436.41 support; after holding above it, look for 2,484.62. $ETH #ETH

ETH rallies 30% in a week—leaving Bitcoin in the dust. In seven days ETH is up 29.8%, while Bitcoin is only up 22.9%. On Saturday it surged straight to $2,546. A week ago it was still hovering around $1,800, playing dead. This comeback has been executed beautifully.

The trigger is just three words: “out of stock.” The data speaks for itself. On exchanges, the amount of ETH is down 15% from early June, falling from 7.7 million coins to 6.54 million. In addition, 42 million coins are locked in staking, accounting for one-third of the total supply—so the amount of sellable ETH available at any moment is getting smaller. When buyers push hard, the price feels like it’s taking off on a rocket.

Liquidity also cooperates. Ethereum spot ETFs saw net inflows of $697 million over the week. Just from the 19th to the 21st—three days—they pulled in $189 million, $221 million, and $185 million respectively. This is the strongest wave since last October. BlackRock led the buying, and the Wall Street demand is far more aggressive than retail.

The worst off are the derivatives traders. In the past 24 hours, the entire market liquidated positions totaling $1.21 billion, with ETH accounting for $265 million. More than 230,000 traders were forced out. Shorts were blown up, and the long positions that chased higher got flushed too. Both sides took hits—this is the cost of leverage.

My take: this ETH move is different from Bitcoin’s. It has staking locks, continuous ETF buying, and an ecosystem narrative. For the short term, a pullback to around 2400 is fine—as long as it doesn’t break. The trend is still there. But remember: after a +30% rally, chasing is always the most uncomfortable position. If you want to get on board, wait for a pullback—don’t follow the crowd. Also, this wave has pushed ETH’s market-cap share back to 11%, keeping it firmly in second place.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury ups the ante on Iran tomorrow: the largest financial blockade in history—why is BTC trembling first?

The U.S. Department of the Treasury will launch the largest-scale financial sanctions against Iran tomorrow. Geopolitical risks are escalating, and the near-term outlook is bearish for the crypto market.

The U.S. Department of the Treasury announced that it will initiate a so-called “largest-ever financial offensive” against Iran tomorrow. The core is to further tighten the blockade on Iran’s oil exports and its financial system, cutting off its external funding channels. In plain terms, it means upgrading sanctions from “targeted strikes” to “a full-scale encirclement.” The issue is that Iran’s diplomatic and nuclear negotiation leverage will be further compressed, and the probability of retaliation actually rises—this Middle East powder keg is again likely to start smoking.

Market impact
Specific transmission path: escalation of geopolitical conflict → broad pressure on risk assets → the crypto market, as a high-volatility asset, is hit first. Historically, whenever the Middle East situation tightens, BTC tends to drop first on the short term. The 2019 U.S.-Iran standoff episode, where BTC fell more than 5% within 24 hours, is not without precedent.

- Short term: safe-haven sentiment heats up; funds rotate from high-beta assets like BTC and ETH into gold and U.S. Treasuries. BTC is currently at $77,501.3, up only 0.64% in the past 24 hours. Once the selloff driven by safe-haven demand materializes, support around the $75,000 level will be directly tested. ETH is currently at $2,452.02, up 1.49% over the past 24 hours; the gains are likely to be given back.
- Medium term: if the sanctions escalation pushes oil prices higher → U.S. inflation expectations rebound → the Fed’s rate-cut timeline is delayed—this chain is likely to be more persistent in its impact on crypto valuations than the event itself.

My view
I’m bearish in the short term. If BTC’s $75,000 support fails after the sanctions are implemented tomorrow, the next stop is around $72,000. ETH is relatively weaker; $2,380 is the key line of defense. Be alert for reversal signals: if Iran responds with restraint and only fights verbally, safe-haven sentiment will quickly fade, and the rebound could be swift. Drawdowns driven by geopolitical events usually come hard and go hard too. The key is not to chase shorts when panic selling starts.

- Direction: bearish 📉 predicted drop

美国财政部明天对伊朗放大招：史上最大规模金融封锁，为什么BTC先瑟瑟发抖？

美国财政部明日启动对伊朗最大规模金融制裁，地缘风险升级，短期利空加密市场。

美国财政部宣布，明天将对伊朗发动所谓“史上最大规模的金融攻势”，核心是进一步收紧对伊朗石油出口和金融体系的封锁，切断其外部资金通道。说白了，就是把制裁从“定点打击”升级成“全面围堵”。问题在于，伊朗手里的外交和核谈判筹码会被进一步压缩，反击的概率反而在上升——中东这个火药桶又要冒烟了。

对市场的影响
具体传导路径：地缘冲突升级 → 风险资产整体承压 → 加密市场作为高波动资产首当其冲。历史上每次中东局势紧张，BTC短线都是先跌为敬，2019年美伊对抗时24小时内跌超5%的剧本不是没演过。

- 短期：避险情绪升温，资金从BTC、ETH等高β资产流向黄金和美债。BTC现报$77,501.3，24h仅微涨0.64%，一旦避险抛压落地，$75,000一线支撑将直接受考验。ETH现报$2,452.02，24h涨1.49%，涨幅大概率回吐。

While Bitcoin grabbed every headline this week, the second-largest crypto quietly did something more unusual: it out-ran BTC, day after day, in the same rally.

Ethereum has surged roughly 18-22% over the past week, briefly touching a two-week high near $2,517 with ETH spot ETFs pulling in $189 million in a single day — the largest inflow in months, right alongside Bitcoin's own record haul. Analyst Michaël van de Poppe flagged the move publicly, noting ETH climbing faster than BTC and sweeping toward key BTC-denominated ratio levels — the kind of relative strength some read as an early alt-season signal.

The 4H chart shows the anatomy of the move clearly: after weeks of consolidation, ETH broke out with a large green candle, climbing steadily through its EMAs to a local high, before pulling back slightly to its current $2,472.72 — sitting almost exactly on the $2,400 "golden pocket" Fibonacci level that's acted as the pivot for this entire leg. RSI sits at 72.02, just as overbought as Bitcoin's reading, and the MACD histogram is negative at -14.09, the same momentum-fading signature showing up here too.

ETH outperforming BTC during a rally is genuinely one of the more reliable early signs of capital rotating into altcoins — that part of the story checks out technically, not just anecdotally. But the same overbought RSI and negative MACD divergence sitting on both charts right now means the fatigue isn't unique to Bitcoin; it's market-wide. As CoinDesk noted about this same move, a single day of ETF inflows confirms a breakout — it doesn't confirm it'll last. Whether ETH holds this golden pocket level or gives it back decides which story wins.

Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

对市场的影响
- 短期：地缘冲突对BTC历来是双刃，但2022年以来的规律很清楚——冲突初期先跌，避险资金先去黄金和美债，BTC要等恐慌峰值过后才轮到反弹。传导路径：油价上涨 → 通胀预期升温 → 降息预期推迟 → ETF资金流入放缓 → BTC直接失去最重要的买盘支撑。ETH $2,460.3 跟跌弹性更大，24h涨1.86%这点涨幅大概率吐回去。
- 中期：如果伊朗封锁霍尔木兹海峡的极端情景出现，全球风险资产集体去杠杆，加密市场作为高贝塔资产跑不掉。中美关系若因伊朗问题进一步紧张，稳定币和合规通道也可能受牵连。

我的判断
短期看空，不装。BTC守不守得住 $75,000 是关键，跌破这个位置下一站看 $72,000 一带。地缘黑天鹅的特点是消息驱动的插针行情，波动率会先起来，方向往下。ETH杠杆更高，$2,400 一破回撤会比BTC深。这波不适合赌反弹，等恐慌情绪见顶的信号再说。

27%！SPK这涨幅，说实话我也没想到能这么猛，直接给我整不会了。别问我怎么知道的，早上刷行情的时候差点把咖啡喷屏幕上。

先说说今天的山寨行情，那真是红红火火恍恍惚惚。SPK拉了27个点，MORPHO紧跟其后26%，GRASS也22%跟上，这仨今天就是主角，没跑。我看了下数据，SPK现在0.0224，24h高点0.02393，低点0.0158，当前价格在区间81%的位置。关键是放量了，3.9倍均量，这个就很有说服力。之前关注这个币的时候还是小透明，现在直接爆发，让我想起上个月错过的那波，说多了都是泪啊。

MORPHO这个更夸张，2.83，直接顶到区间98%的位置，离24h高点就一步之遥。2.5倍放量，资金费率0.005%正常，没有过热迹象。讲真，这种贴脸阻力的走势，要么直接突破新高，要么就是冲高回落，很考验心态。GRASS也是98%位置，0.3628，2.7倍量能，资金费率0.0141%稍微高一点点，但还在正常范围。

那咱来说点能落地的交易思路。短线视角，SPK偏多方向，回踩0.01975-0.0200区间可以考虑，止损放0.0185下方，第一目标0.02393，盈亏比大概1:3左右，挺香的。但要注意，如果跌破0.01975且放量，那这个判断就失效了，别硬扛。MORPHO的话，2.593是近8根支撑，回踩这个位置偏多思路，止损2.48，目标2.848，RR大概1:2.5。GRASS就看0.3201支撑，止损0.30，目标0.3641，RR也有1:2.8的样子。这些都是短线思路哈，中线的话等回调再考虑，别追高。

量价配合这块，SPK和GRASS都是放量上涨，可信度比较高。但我得提醒一句，冲高回落留长上影的情况要小心追高，别到时候又吃个大亏（是的我就是这么贪心过）。资金费率方面，GRASS的0.0141%稍微偏高了点，多头有点拥挤，如果价格冲高但费率继续飙，那就要警惕了。

恐惧贪婪指数50，中性位置，不算极端。BTC周涨22.7%，ETH周涨30%，大盘情绪明显回暖。这种时候，我觉得可以保持一定仓位，但别梭哈，毕竟山寨币波动大，小心驶得万年船。PENGU、TRUMP这些也都涨了快20%，市场整体都在嗨。

对了，跌幅榜那边MAGMA跌了13.6%，US跌了12%，资金明显在从这些板块流向涨幅榜，板块轮动的味道很浓。热搜榜全是meme币，CATALORIAN、CYBERLEEK这些，讲真我看着名字都觉得有点离谱，但离谱在这个市场就是合理的（手动狗头）。

Why is the EU targeting DeFi vaults? MiCA’s new rules focus on crypto lending

💡 Impact assessment: Neutral-to-bearish in the short term; regulatory expansion is a long-term negative signal for DeFi.

On May 20, the EU launched a consultation to assess whether crypto lending and DeFi vaults should be brought under MiCA regulation, with a deadline of September 30.

What’s going on
When MiCA was legislated in 2023, it intentionally left loopholes: crypto lending was completely excluded, and certain partially decentralized activities were also excluded. Now Brussels wants to close those gaps. The European Commission has initiated a targeted consultation, with DeFi lending vaults (vaults) being the main gray-area focus.

European digital asset lawyer Yuriy Brisov put it plainly: EU law does not recognize “vaults” as an independent category. In other words, the regulatory framework is still stuck in the era of centralized exchanges, even though funds have already moved on-chain. Once brought under MiCA, the operators of these vaults will likely have to be treated like service providers—licenses and compliance costs will be unavoidable.

Market impact
- Short term: The news itself isn’t new; the consultation period runs until late September, so there’s no immediate execution or “kill shot.” BTC is currently $93,85 032.35, up 0.22% slightly; ETH at $2,437.89 is up 1.15%. The market basically isn’t reacting. But sentiment toward the DeFi sector is under pressure, and compliance expectations for European projects may be discounted first.
- Medium term: This is part of a global trend— the U.S. is setting up DeFi reporting requirements, while the EU is closing gaps in MiCA. The narrative of decentralized “lawless zones” is being systematically dismantled. European vault-type protocols will either comply or leave the EU market; liquidity fragmentation is hard to avoid.

My view
In the short term, I’d wait. In the medium term, DeFi is bearish. The consultation deadline is still about four months away; the real “shoe drop” depends on the legislative timeline in 2027. In the meantime, every development is likely to weigh on DeFi token valuations. For BTC, it’s consolidating around the $93.85K range without a catalyst for a breakdown due to this news. ETH is holding up relatively better, but the DeFi TVL logic is being tested. Risk point: if the consultation results lean toward fully bringing everything under scope, major European lending protocols may pull some products early.

One-sentence translation: Decentralization no longer means being free from regulation—it just means the bill arrives later.

A new study by three Vietnamese researchers: as EU carbon prices rise, mining activity really shifts to cheaper places like Russia.

This research measures the relationship between EU carbon emissions pricing and so-called “carbon leakage.” The conclusion is straightforward: the higher the price of carbon allowances, the more some Bitcoin mining tends to relocate to areas with looser regulation and cheaper energy—such as Russia—purely to maximize profit. In other words, mining rigs don’t recognize borders: wherever electricity is cheaper, they move there. This isn’t speculation—the data show a positive correlation between carbon prices and mining migration.

One-sentence translation: carbon taxes haven’t eliminated the carbon emissions from mining; they’ve just moved those emissions elsewhere.

- Short term: almost no effect on the coin price. BTC is still trading sideways near $77,032.35, with only a 0.22% move over 24h. The geographic distribution of mining is a slow variable—it won’t cause liquidations or trigger FOMO.
- Mid term: this is a line worth watching. Ongoing regulatory pressure in Europe and the U.S. will likely further concentrate computing power in Russia and Central Asia, strengthening the political narrative that “Bitcoin mining is not eco-friendly + involves geopolitical risk,” and providing ammunition for future regulation. Resistance to ESG capital entering the market may increase.

Slightly bullish, leaning neutral. The logic is simple: computing power migration doesn’t affect BTC’s supply schedule (difficulty adjusts automatically); the price’s core driver is still liquidity. #dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  This batch of on-chain data revealed a frustrating loophole involving @Dusk_Foundation . This isn’t an exaggeration: due to a misreading of a certain underlying metric, the on-chain earnings of $DUSK  have been artificially amplified by as much as 25x on some tracking platforms.

Here’s what happened. When I went through W3sper’s on-chain confirmation records, I noticed a value called gasPaid. My first intuition was probably the same as most people’s: surely this number only represents the amount of gas consumed, and you’d need to multiply it by the current gas price to get the exact cost. Fortunately, I checked the source code—W3sper had already settled the bill. The parameter it returns is the final deducted total amount of LUX.

In other words, gasPaid is essentially gas_spent multiplied by gas_price. But if an external scraping script doesn’t know this and multiplies by unit price again, the whole calculation formula gets distorted: it turns into gas_spent multiplied by the square of gas_price. That’s not a small error. For example, if during a congestion period the gas price jumps from 1 to 5, the real on-chain fee only increases by 5x; but on charts with incorrect logic, it can misleadingly show an insane 25x surge. The more congested the network is, the more dramatic the visual illusion becomes.

This “good news” looks clean at the code level and especially pretty on the interface, but it can seriously harm people. On one hand, high-frequency quant bots that call these distorted parameters may conclude the transaction wear-and-tear is too high, and automatically raise their entry thresholds—filtering out a large number of otherwise risk-free spread opportunities. On the other hand, if analysts across the board only look at these fake earnings spike curves, they’ll very likely raise expectations for DUSK as a matter of course. All because they failed to understand the measurement of a single field, and both trading strategies and fundamental assessments end up backfiring.

I’ve finally made it clear to myself: don’t easily trust those flashy charts. To find the truth, you must stick to the hard facts and do cross-checking—exactly how much LUX a wallet is missing, how much gas_spent is in the underlying records, and what the instantaneous gas price actually is. If these three numbers don’t line up, even a beautifully drawn K-line chart wouldn’t make me believe it. At the end of the day, DUSK’s value capture has to come from real, tangible, effective interactions. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  这次盘数据，在 @Dusk_Foundation 身上抓到了个让人相当无语的漏洞。这不是危言耸听：由于某项底层指标被误读，$DUSK 的链上收益在部分追踪平台里，硬生生给放大了25倍之多。

事情是这样的，当我去扒 W3sper 的链上确认记录时，注意到了 gasPaid 这个数值。很多人第一直觉大概跟我一样，以为这玩意仅仅代表“消耗的Gas量”，还得去乘上当前的 Gas Price 才能得出确切花销。好在我留了个心眼，去核对了一下源码，才发现 W3sper 早就把账结清了：该参数返回的就是最终扣除的 LUX 总额。

也就是说，gasPaid 本质上已经是 gas_spent 乘以 gas_price 的结果。但如果外部的抓取脚本不懂行，擅自再乘一次单价，整个计算公式就彻底变形，变成了 gas_spent 乘上 gas_price 的平方。这不是一星半点的误差。打个比方，假如拥堵期 Gas 单价从 1 飙升到 5，真实的链上费用其实也就涨了 5 倍而已；但在那些写错逻辑的图表上，却会呈现出 25 倍的逆天涨幅。网络越卡，这种视觉错觉就越惊人。

这种代码层面没报错、界面上又格外养眼的“好消息”，其实害人不浅。一方面，链上的高频打工仔量化机器人在调取这些失真参数时，会认定交易磨损太高，进而自动调高出手门槛，导致大把原本稳赚的差价机会被白白过滤掉。另一方面，各路分析师如果光看这种虚假的收益猛增曲线，极大概率会顺势推高对DUSK的预期。仅仅因为没搞明白一个字段的度量衡，就让交易策略和基本面研判双双翻车。

我算是彻底认清了：别轻易相信那些华丽的走势图。想弄清真相，必须只认死理进行交叉比对：钱包到底少了多少 LUX、底层记录的 gas_spent 是多少、瞬时的 Gas Price 又处于什么水平。只要这三个数对不上号，K线画出花来我也不敢信。归根结底DUSK的价值捕获，得靠实打实的有效交互来贡献。#eth $ETH

People still waiting for a BTC second dip may be making the biggest mistake of this cycle.

In the past week, BTC jumped directly by about 22.7%, rising $14,264 in a single week.

This is the largest week-over-week U.S. dollar increase in BTC’s history.

But I think the real thing worth watching isn’t the candlestick chart.

It’s the money.

Last week, U.S. BTC spot ETFs saw net inflows of about $1.92 billion, and there were net inflows for five straight trading days.

In total, BTC + ETH ETFs pulled in about $2.62 billion over the week.

The biggest difference from the previous phase of the market is:

Before, many rallies looked more like
short-covering → pushing prices higher via futures → FOMO buyers getting in.

This time, you can start to see:

ETF inflows + spot demand + short squeezes + improved macro liquidity happening at the same time.

That’s more dangerous.

The danger isn’t that BTC has to go down.

Instead, it’s that a lot of people who are still waiting for a “second dip” or “to buy after it drops a bit more” may be getting forced by the market to chase higher prices.

Right now, I’m actually not too fixated on whether BTC is 75K, 77K, or 80K.

What we need to watch next are three things:

1. Can ETFs keep seeing net inflows every day?
2. Is OI starting to rise uncontrollably?
3. Is Funding getting clearly overheated?

If the price rises, ETFs keep bringing in money, but Funding and OI aren’t blowing up wildly:

Then this move is still mainly driven by spot.

That kind of market is the most dangerous.

Because it often doesn’t end after just two days of rally—it tends to keep running until everyone who’s still on the sidelines can’t help but chase in.

But if BTC then surges to 80K+ and OI spikes in sync, while Funding turns extremely positive:

Then I’d start reducing my position.

In a bull market, the easiest time to lose money is never when nobody is bullish.

It’s when everyone suddenly realizes:

“Turns out it really is a bull market.”

You guys think it’s like:

I’m leaning A, but I’ll closely watch OI and Funding.

#BTC   #比特币  #ETH  #crypto

EU wants to fill the regulatory gap for DeFi lending: this time it’s not a ban, but to bring it under MiCA

💡 Slightly bearish to neutral: tighter regulation expectations may weigh on DeFi sentiment in the short term

The European Commission has launched a consultation to assess whether crypto lending and DeFi treasuries should be brought under MiCA regulation, with feedback due by September 30.

What’s going on
On May 20, the EU launched a targeted consultation. The core issue: back when MiCA legislation was being drafted, crypto lending and some exempted partially decentralized activities were intentionally carved out—now should they be regulated after all. The feedback period runs until September 30. EU lawyer Yuriy Brisov highlighted the key point: EU law currently does not even recognize “vault” as a category, meaning many yield-strategy products in DeFi are, under the current framework, essentially operating outside the law.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment is slightly bearish. DeFi will have to go through the old “regulatory uncertainty” playbook again, and funds may temporarily rotate out of smaller DeFi tokens into mainstream assets such as BTC $77,032 and ETH $2,437 for risk hedging. Since ETH serves as the DeFi settlement layer, it is hit more directly by consultation-related news. In the past 24 hours, ETH is up only 1.15%, noticeably weaker than what people had expected from capital rotation.
- Medium term: don’t jump to pessimism. Being included in MiCA doesn’t equal getting shut down. MiCA is a licensing framework—once a compliance pathway is opened, institutional capital has more reasons to enter. What is truly hurt is pure anonymous protocols that cannot meet KYC requirements. September 30 is the key date; before then, it’s likely to remain a choppy, back-and-forth consolidation.

My take
In the short term, I’m more inclined to wait and see with a bearish bias; in the medium term, it’s not necessarily bad. BTC is likely to trade in a narrow range around $77,032 (only +0.22% in 24h). This kind of regulatory headline has limited impact on it, and mainstream coins can hold up. ETH needs to watch the $2,400 area—if it can’t hold, it may see a catch-down move. Volatility in DeFi concept tokens could be amplified, but direction won’t be clear until the details of the consultation documents are finalized. In plain terms: the EU isn’t trying to turn off the lights—it wants to install a power meter. The installation process is uncomfortable, but once it’s done, only then will the official forces dare to move in.

The more the EU carbon tax is collected, the tighter it gets—yet bitcoin mining shifts to Russia instead: what exactly did emissions reduction reduce?

Vietnamese researchers release a study: the higher the EU carbon price, the more mining moves to cheaper regions like Russia.

Three Vietnamese researchers conducted a study and found that EU carbon emission pricing is positively correlated with so-called “carbon leakage.” When carbon allowance prices rise, some bitcoin mining activities relocate to places like Russia—energy is cheaper there and regulatory oversight is more relaxed—so as to maximize profits. Put simply, miners do the math on the electricity bill: they move to where costs are lower. Within the EU, the carbon tax effectively “squeezes” computing power out.

Market impact
- Short term: basically no impact on the BTC price. Computing power migration is a slow variable. BTC is currently $77,032.35, up only 0.22% in the past 24 hours—so the market isn’t treating it as a trading logic.
- Medium term: the value of this study is in the regulatory narrative. It provides policymakers with evidence—unilateral carbon taxes may lead to industry outflows rather than actual emissions reductions. If the EU subsequently strengthens environmental regulations for mining or the crypto industry, “mining shifting to Russia” could become a geopolitical issue, potentially affecting how European institutions view their funding.

My take
I lean slightly neutral-to-bearish, but not on the price level—rather on the narrative level. This study doesn’t change BTC’s direction in the short term; around $77,032, longs and shorts are still grinding. The real risk is this: if Western regulators treat “concentrating hash rate in Russia” as a sanctions breakthrough, and tighten mining regulation as a result—that would be a medium-term negative.

ETH is affected less; at $2,437 it basically follows its own pace. For now, I’d stay on the sidelines and wait to see whether there are any follow-up actions on the regulatory front.

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Lately, I’ve been looking up @Dusk’s fundamental data, and during reconciliation I almost got fooled by some external market-data websites. Today I have to pull this thorn out: when congestion happens, the Gas Price only goes up by 5x, yet on these statistical platforms’ charts the protocol’s total incoming for $DUSK  shows a wildly abnormal 25x surge!

At first, I zeroed in on the gasPaid parameter emitted by the W3sper contract. Following past habits, I assumed most people would think it simply represents the “amount of Gas consumed,” so it would be natural to multiply it again by the real-time Gas unit price. But in the spirit of rigor, I checked the source code—and that’s when it became crystal clear: the value W3sper outputs is actually the total LUX cost after the system has already deducted everything.

That’s incredibly funny, because this field by itself is already gas_spent × gas_price. If an external indexing tool blindly follows the same pattern, takes this number and multiplies by the unit price again, the formula directly becomes gas_spent × gas_price². Plug in some numbers and you’ll see how absurd it gets: suppose the chain is congested and the unit price jumps from 1 to 5—then the real fees are only 5x. But on those “miscalculated-accounting” platforms, they still manage to render a 25x “income illusion” for you. The more crowded the network, the higher that chart flies.

This quiet, silent computation bug is extremely dangerous. First, it targets bots running high-frequency strategies—when their programs read such an exaggerated cost estimate, they immediately raise the arbitrage lower bound, causing countless money-making opportunities that could have been captured to be discarded. Second, it also targets people doing investment research: once they see this god-tier “network income” curve, they’re very likely to get hotheaded and slap an utterly unreasonable premium on DUSK. All because one parameter wasn’t understood, both the trading model and the fundamental valuation end up as the biggest fools.

To verify whether the data has been inflated, I only look at three hard proofs now: the LUX balance actually deducted in the wallet address, the most original gas_spent from the underlying logs, and the instantaneous real Gas Price. If these three don’t add up, no matter how “divine” the chart looks, I won’t believe it. For DUSK, the rise in fees must rely on a genuine increase in real activity. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation 最近在查阅 @Dusk 的基本面数据，结果对账的时候差点被某些外部行情网站给忽悠瘸了。今天必须来拔个草：明明遇到拥堵时 Gas Price 只是拉高了 5 倍，但在这些统计平台的图表里，$DUSK 的协议总进账居然呈现出 25 倍的变态级暴涨！

刚开始盯上 W3sper 合约里抛出的 gasPaid 参数时，按照过往的惯性思维，估计很多人都以为这仅仅代表“消耗掉的Gas额度”，理所当然地觉得还得再乘一次实时 Gas 单价。但本着严谨的态度我去查了源码，这一下彻底破案了：W3sper 吐出来的这个值，压根就是系统已经扣除完毕的 LUX 开销总和。

这就非常搞笑了，因为这个字段本身已经是 gas_spent × gas_price。要是外部的索引工具照猫画虎，拿到这个数字后不管三七二十一又去乘一次单价，公式就直接畸变成了 gas_spent × gas_price²。大家稍微代入下数字就知道有多离谱：假设链上卡顿，单价从 1 变成 5，真实的手续费其实也就翻了 5 倍；结果在那些算糊涂账的平台上，硬是能给你渲染出 25 倍的“收入假象”。网络越拥挤，这图表就越是往天上飞。

这种闷声不响的计算 BUG，杀伤力极其恐怖。一来是坑了跑高频策略的机器人，程序一读到这么夸张的成本预估，立马吓得调高套利下限，导致大把原本可以捡钱的机会被白白扔掉；二来更是坑了做投研的人，一看到这种逆天的“网络收入”曲线，很容易脑热给DUSK披上一层极其不合理的溢价。就因为一个参数没搞懂，让交易模型和基本面估值双双成了大冤种。

想验证数据有没有注水，我如今只看三处铁证：钱包地址里实打实被扣除的 LUX 余额、底层日志里最原始的 gas_spent、外加瞬时的真实 Gas Price。要是这三笔账对不上，图表画得再神我也坚决不信。对DUSK而言，费用的上涨必须仰仗真实活跃度的提升。#eth $ETH
